works.author: Almeida Garrett
works.title: This hell of loving
works.scope: Complete · 18 lines, three six-line stanzas
works.scope_es: Completo · 18 versos, tres sextillas
works.source_edition: Folhas Caídas, 1853, via pt.wikisource.
works.source_edition_es: Folhas Caídas, 1853, vía pt.wikisource.
works.note: Three stanzas of questions with no answers. The poem does not resolve; it stops at the moment the speaker began to live.
works.note_es: Tres estrofas de preguntas sin respuesta. El poema no se resuelve: se detiene en el instante en que el que habla empezó a vivir.

segments.original: Este inferno de amar - como eu amo! –
segments.es: Este infierno de amar —¡como yo amo!—,
segments.en: This hell of loving - as I love! -

segments.original: Quem mo pôs aqui n'alma ... quem foi?
segments.es: ¿quién me lo puso aquí en el alma... quién fue?
segments.en: who put it here in my soul ... who was it?

segments.original: Esta chama que alenta e consome,
segments.es: Esta llama que alienta y consume,
segments.en: This flame that sustains and consumes,

segments.original: Que é a vida - e que a vida destrói –
segments.es: que es la vida —y que la vida destruye—,
segments.en: which is life - and which destroys life -

segments.original: Como é que se veio a atear,
segments.es: ¿cómo llegó a prenderse,
segments.en: how did it come to be kindled,

segments.original: Quando - ai quando se há-de ela apagar?
segments.es: cuándo —ay, cuándo— habrá de apagarse?
segments.en: when - ah, when is it to go out?

segments.original: Eu não sei, não me lembra: o passado,
segments.es: Yo no sé, no me acuerdo: el pasado,
segments.en: I do not know, I do not remember: the past,

segments.original: A outra vida que dantes vivi
segments.es: la otra vida que antes viví
segments.en: the other life that I lived before

segments.original: Era um sonho talvez... - foi um sonho-
segments.es: era un sueño tal vez... fue un sueño.
segments.en: was a dream perhaps... - it was a dream -

segments.original: Em que paz tão serena a dormi!
segments.es: ¡En qué paz tan serena la dormí!
segments.en: in what serene peace I slept it through!

segments.original: Oh!, que doce era aquele sonhar ...
segments.es: ¡Oh, qué dulce era aquel soñar...!
segments.en: Oh, how sweet that dreaming was ...

segments.original: Quem me veio, ai de mim!, despertar?
segments.es: ¿Quién vino, ay de mí, a despertarme?
segments.en: Who came, alas, to wake me?

segments.original: Só me lembra que um dia formoso
segments.es: Sólo recuerdo que un día hermoso
segments.en: I only remember that on a fine day

segments.original: Eu passei... dava o Sol tanta luz!
segments.es: pasé... ¡daba el Sol tanta luz!
segments.en: I passed by... the Sun gave so much light!

segments.original: E os meus olhos, que vagos giravam,
segments.es: Y mis ojos, que vagos giraban,
segments.en: And my eyes, which were idly wandering,

segments.original: Em seus olhos ardentes os pus.
segments.es: en sus ojos ardientes los puse.
segments.en: I fixed upon her burning eyes.

segments.original: Que fez ela?, eu que fiz? - Não no sei;
segments.es: ¿Qué hizo ella? ¿Yo qué hice? No lo sé;
segments.en: What did she do? What did I do? I do not know;

segments.original: Mas nessa hora a viver comecei ...
segments.es: mas en esa hora a vivir comencé...
segments.en: but in that hour I began to live ...

works.translation_credit: New AI working translation for Katabasis; not a published literary translation.

works.author: Antero de Quental
works.title: In the hand of God
works.scope: Complete · sonnet, 14 lines (printed dedication not included)
works.scope_es: Completo · soneto, 14 versos (no se incluye la dedicatoria impresa)
works.source_edition: Os sonetos completos de Antero de Quental. The sonnet carries a printed dedication, 'Á Ex.ma Snr.ª Victoria de O. M.'.
works.source_edition_es: Os sonetos completos de Antero de Quental. El soneto lleva impresa una dedicatoria, «Á Ex.ma Snr.ª Victoria de O. M.».
works.note: The poet comes down from the palace of Illusion and asks his heart to sleep. He took his own life a few years after writing it.
works.note_es: El poeta baja del palacio de la Ilusión y le pide a su corazón que duerma. Se quitó la vida pocos años después de escribirlo.

segments.original: Na mão de Deus, na sua mão direita,
segments.es: En la mano de Dios, en su mano derecha,
segments.en: In the hand of God, in his right hand,

segments.original: Descansou afinal meu coração.
segments.es: descansó al fin mi corazón.
segments.en: my heart has rested at last.

segments.original: Do palácio encantado da Ilusão
segments.es: Del palacio encantado de la Ilusión
segments.en: From the enchanted palace of Illusion

segments.original: Desci a passo e passo a escada estreita.
segments.es: bajé paso a paso la escalera estrecha.
segments.en: I came down step by step the narrow stair.

segments.original: Como as flores mortais, com que se enfeita
segments.es: Como las flores mortales con que se adorna
segments.en: Like the mortal flowers with which

segments.original: A ignorância infantil, despôjo vão,
segments.es: la ignorancia infantil, despojo vano,
segments.en: childish ignorance decks itself, a vain spoil,

segments.original: Depus do Ideal e da Paixão
segments.es: dejé del Ideal y de la Pasión
segments.en: I laid aside of the Ideal and of Passion

segments.original: A forma transitória e imperfeita.
segments.es: la forma transitoria e imperfecta.
segments.en: the transitory and imperfect form.

segments.original: Como criança, em lôbrega jornada,
segments.es: Como el niño que, en lóbrega jornada,
segments.en: Like a child, on a gloomy journey,

segments.original: Que a mãe leva ao colo agasalhada
segments.es: la madre lleva en brazos, abrigado,
segments.en: whom the mother carries wrapped in her arms

segments.original: E atravessa, sorrindo vagamente,
segments.es: y atraviesa, sonriendo vagamente,
segments.en: and crosses, smiling vaguely,

segments.original: Selvas, mares, areias do deserto...
segments.es: selvas, mares, arenas del desierto...
segments.en: forests, seas, sands of the desert...

segments.original: Dorme o teu sono, coração liberto,
segments.es: duerme tu sueño, corazón liberto,
segments.en: sleep your sleep, liberated heart,

segments.original: Dorme na mão de Deus eternamente!
segments.es: ¡duerme en la mano de Dios eternamente!
segments.en: sleep in the hand of God eternally!

works.translation_credit: New AI working translation for Katabasis; not a published literary translation.

works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.title: The dream of the burning heart
works.scope: Vita nuova, III · complete chapter, with its sonnet
works.scope_es: Vita nuova, III · capítulo completo, con su soneto
works.source_edition: Dante Alighieri, La Vita Nuova, critical edition by Michele Barbi (Florence, Società Dantesca Italiana, 1907), Italian Wikisource. Footnote markers removed; three evident transcription slips corrected: se non poche, che in mano, fare uno sonetto.
works.source_edition_es: Dante Alighieri, La Vita Nuova, edición crítica de Michele Barbi (Florencia, Società Dantesca Italiana, 1907), Wikisource en italiano. Se quitan las llamadas de nota y se corrigen tres erratas evidentes de la transcripción: se non poche, che in mano, fare uno sonetto.
works.note: Nine years after first seeing her, Dante receives Beatrice’s greeting in the street and that night dreams that Love makes her eat his burning heart. He sent the sonnet about the dream to the poets of Florence; the one he calls the first of his friends, Guido Cavalcanti, answered it.
works.note_es: Nueve años después de verla por primera vez, Dante recibe en la calle el saludo de Beatriz y esa noche sueña que Amor le da a comer su corazón ardiente. Envió el soneto del sueño a los poetas de Florencia; le respondió el que llama el primero de sus amigos, Guido Cavalcanti.

segments.original: Poi che fuoro passati tanti die, che appunto erano compiuti li nove anni appresso l'apparimento soprascritto di questa gentilissima, ne l'ultimo di questi die avenne che questa mirabile donna apparve a me, vestita di colore bianchissimo, in mezzo di due gentili donne, le quali erano di più lunga etade;
segments.es: Cuando hubieron pasado tantos días que se cumplían justamente nueve años desde la aparición de esta gentilísima que conté antes, en el último de esos días sucedió que esta mujer admirable se me apareció vestida de un blanco purísimo, entre dos nobles damas de más edad;
segments.en: When so many days had passed that exactly nine years were complete since the appearance of this most gracious lady told above, on the last of those days it happened that this wondrous lady appeared to me, dressed in purest white, between two noble ladies older than she;

segments.original: e passando per una via, volse li occhi verso quella parte ov’io era molto pauroso, e per la sua ineffabile cortesia, la quale è oggi meritata nel grande secolo, mi salutoe molto virtuosamente, tanto che me parve allora vedere tutti li termini de la beatitudine.
segments.es: y al pasar por una calle volvió los ojos hacia donde yo estaba, muy temeroso, y por su inefable cortesía, que hoy recibe su premio en el gran siglo, me saludó con tanta virtud que me pareció ver entonces todos los confines de la bienaventuranza.
segments.en: and passing along a street she turned her eyes toward where I stood, full of fear, and by her ineffable courtesy, which today has its reward in the great world beyond, she greeted me with such grace that I seemed then to see all the bounds of blessedness.

segments.original: L’ora che lo suo dolcissimo salutare mi giunse, era fermamente nona di quello giorno;
segments.es: La hora en que me llegó su dulcísimo saludo era, con certeza, la hora nona de aquel día;
segments.en: The hour when her sweetest greeting reached me was certainly the ninth of that day;

segments.original: e però che quella fu la prima volta che le sue parole si mossero per venire a li miei orecchi, presi tanta dolcezza, che come inebriato mi partio da le genti, e ricorsi a lo solingo luogo d’una mia camera, e puosimi a pensare di questa cortesissima.
segments.es: y como aquella fue la primera vez que sus palabras se movieron para llegar a mis oídos, sentí tanta dulzura que, como embriagado, me aparté de la gente, me refugié en la soledad de mi cuarto y me puse a pensar en esta cortesísima.
segments.en: and since that was the first time her words had moved to reach my ears, I felt such sweetness that, as if drunk, I left the company of people, took refuge in the solitude of my room, and began to think of this most courteous lady.

segments.original: E pensando di lei mi sopragiunse uno soave sonno, ne lo quale m’apparve una maravigliosa visione,
segments.es: Y pensando en ella me sobrevino un sueño suave, en el que se me apareció una visión maravillosa:
segments.en: And as I thought of her a gentle sleep came over me, in which a marvellous vision appeared to me:

segments.original: che me parea vedere ne la mia camera una nebula di colore di fuoco, dentro a la quale io discernea una figura d’uno segnore di pauroso aspetto a chi la guardasse;
segments.es: me parecía ver en mi cuarto una nube del color del fuego, y dentro de ella distinguía la figura de un señor de aspecto temible para quien lo mirara;
segments.en: I seemed to see in my room a cloud the colour of fire, and within it I made out the figure of a lord, fearful to whoever looked on him;

segments.original: e pareami con tanta letizia, quanto a sè, che mirabile cosa era; e ne le sue parole dicea molte cose, le quali io non intendea se non poche; tra le quali intendea queste: «Ego dominus tuus».
segments.es: y me parecía, en sí mismo, tan lleno de alegría que era cosa admirable; y en sus palabras decía muchas cosas, de las que yo entendía solo unas pocas; entre ellas entendía estas: «Yo soy tu señor».
segments.en: and he seemed, in himself, so full of joy that it was a marvel; and in his words he said many things, of which I understood only a few; among them I understood these: “I am your lord.”

segments.original: Ne le sue braccia mi parea vedere una persona dormire nuda, salvo che involta mi parea in uno drappo sanguigno leggeramente;
segments.es: En sus brazos me parecía ver a una persona que dormía desnuda, salvo que me parecía envuelta levemente en un paño color de sangre;
segments.en: In his arms I seemed to see a person sleeping naked, except that she seemed lightly wrapped in a blood-red cloth;

segments.original: la quale io riguardando molto intentivamente, conobbi ch’era la donna de la salute, la quale m’avea lo giorno dinanzi degnato di salutare.
segments.es: y mirándola muy atentamente, reconocí que era la dama del saludo, la que el día antes se había dignado saludarme.
segments.en: and gazing at her very intently, I knew she was the lady of the greeting, who the day before had deigned to greet me.

segments.original: E ne l'una de le mani mi parea che questi tenesse una cosa, la quale ardesse tutta; e pareami che mi dicesse queste parole: «Vide cor tuum».
segments.es: Y en una de las manos me parecía que él sostenía una cosa que ardía entera; y me parecía que me decía estas palabras: «Mira tu corazón».
segments.en: And in one of his hands he seemed to hold something that was all ablaze; and he seemed to say these words to me: “Behold your heart.”

segments.original: E quando elli era stato alquanto, pareami che disvegliasse questa che dormia, e tanto si sforzava per suo ingegno, che le facea mangiare questa cosa che in mano li ardea, la quale ella mangiava dubitosamente.
segments.es: Y cuando había estado así un rato, me parecía que despertaba a la que dormía, y tanto se esforzaba con su ingenio que le hacía comer aquella cosa que le ardía en la mano, y ella la comía con recelo.
segments.en: And when he had stayed so a while, he seemed to wake the sleeper, and he strove so hard with his skill that he made her eat the thing that burned in his hand, and she ate it fearfully.

segments.original: Appresso ciò, poco dimorava che la sua letizia si convertia in amarissimo pianto;
segments.es: Después de esto, su alegría tardaba poco en convertirse en un llanto amarguísimo;
segments.en: After this it was not long before his joy turned into bitterest weeping;

segments.original: e così piangendo, si ricogliea questa donna ne le sue braccia, e con essa mi parea che si ne gisse verso lo cielo;
segments.es: y así, llorando, recogía a esta dama en sus brazos, y me parecía que con ella se iba hacia el cielo;
segments.en: and weeping so, he gathered this lady into his arms, and with her he seemed to go away toward heaven;

segments.original: onde io sostenea sì grande angoscia, che lo mio deboletto sonno non poteo sostenere, anzi si ruppe e fui disvegliato.
segments.es: por lo que yo sentía una angustia tan grande que mi débil sueño no pudo soportarla, sino que se rompió y desperté.
segments.en: at which I felt such anguish that my frail sleep could not bear it, but broke, and I awoke.

segments.original: E mantenente cominciai a pensare, e trovai che l’ora ne la quale m’era questa visione apparita, era la quarta de la notte stata;
segments.es: Y enseguida empecé a pensar, y hallé que la hora en que se me había aparecido esta visión había sido la cuarta de la noche;
segments.en: And at once I began to think, and found that the hour in which this vision had appeared to me had been the fourth of the night;

segments.original: sì che appare manifestamente ch’ella fue la prima ora de le nove ultime ore de la notte.
segments.es: de modo que es evidente que fue la primera de las nueve últimas horas de la noche.
segments.en: so that it plainly appears it was the first of the last nine hours of the night.

segments.original: Pensando io a ciò che m’era apparato, propuosi di farlo sentire a molti, li quali erano famosi trovatori in quello tempo:
segments.es: Pensando en lo que se me había aparecido, me propuse darlo a conocer a muchos que eran trovadores famosos en aquel tiempo;
segments.en: Thinking over what had appeared to me, I resolved to make it known to many who were famous poets at that time;

segments.original: e con ciò fosse cosa che io avesse già veduto per me medesimo l’arte del dire parole per rima, propuosi di fare uno sonetto, ne lo quale io salutasse tutti li fedeli d’Amore;
segments.es: y como yo ya había aprendido por mí mismo el arte de decir palabras en rima, me propuse hacer un soneto en el que saludara a todos los fieles de Amor;
segments.en: and since I had already learned by myself the art of putting words into rhyme, I resolved to write a sonnet greeting all Love’s faithful;

segments.original: e pregandoli che giudicassero la mia visione, scrissi a loro ciò che io avea nel mio sonno veduto. E cominciai allora questo sonetto, lo quale comincia: A ciascun’alma presa.
segments.es: y rogándoles que juzgaran mi visión, les escribí lo que había visto en mi sueño. Y comencé entonces este soneto, que empieza: A cada alma presa.
segments.en: and asking them to judge my vision, I wrote to them what I had seen in my sleep. And I began then this sonnet, which begins: To every captive soul.

segments.original: A ciascun’alma presa e gentil core
segments.es: A cada alma presa y corazón gentil
segments.en: To every captive soul and gentle heart

segments.original: nel cui cospetto ven lo dir presente,
segments.es: ante cuya presencia llegan estas palabras,
segments.en: into whose sight these present words may come,

segments.original: in ciò che mi rescrivan suo parvente,
segments.es: para que me respondan su parecer,
segments.en: so that they write back to me what they think,

segments.original: salute in lor segnor, cioè Amore.
segments.es: salud en su señor, que es Amor.
segments.en: greeting in their lord, that is, Love.

segments.original: Già eran quasi che aterzate l’ore
segments.es: Ya casi había pasado un tercio de las horas
segments.en: A third of the hours had almost passed

segments.original: del tempo che onne stella n’è lucente,
segments.es: del tiempo en que toda estrella nos luce,
segments.en: of the time when every star shines on us,

segments.original: quando m’apparve Amor subitamente,
segments.es: cuando Amor se me apareció de repente,
segments.en: when Love appeared to me suddenly,

segments.original: cui essenza membrar mi dà orrore.
segments.es: cuya esencia me horroriza recordar.
segments.en: whose being I shudder to recall.

segments.original: Allegro mi sembrava Amor tenendo
segments.es: Alegre me parecía Amor, sosteniendo
segments.en: Joyful Love seemed to me, holding

segments.original: meo core in mano, e ne le braccia avea
segments.es: mi corazón en la mano, y en los brazos tenía
segments.en: my heart in his hand, and in his arms he had

segments.original: madonna involta in un drappo dormendo;
segments.es: a mi señora envuelta en un paño, dormida;
segments.en: my lady wrapped in a cloth, asleep;

segments.original: poi la svegliava, e d’esto core ardendo
segments.es: luego la despertaba, y de este corazón ardiente
segments.en: then he woke her, and with this burning heart

segments.original: lei paventosa umilmente pascea:
segments.es: a ella, temerosa, humildemente alimentaba:
segments.en: he humbly fed her, full of fear:

segments.original: appresso gir lo ne vedea piangendo.
segments.es: después lo veía irse llorando.
segments.en: afterward I saw him go away weeping.

segments.original: Questo sonetto si divide in due parti; che ne la prima parte saluto e domando risponsione, ne la seconda significo a che si dee rispondere. La seconda parte comincia quivi: Già eran.
segments.es: Este soneto se divide en dos partes: en la primera saludo y pido respuesta; en la segunda indico a qué se debe responder. La segunda parte comienza aquí: Ya casi.
segments.en: This sonnet is divided into two parts: in the first I greet and ask for an answer; in the second I show what must be answered. The second part begins here: A third.

segments.original: A questo sonetto fue risposto da molti e di diverse sentenzie; tra li quali fue risponditore quelli cui io chiamo primo de li miei amici, e disse allora uno sonetto, lo quale comincia: Vedesti al mio parere onne valore.
segments.es: A este soneto respondieron muchos, con diversos pareceres; entre ellos respondió aquel a quien llamo el primero de mis amigos, y escribió entonces un soneto que comienza: Viste, a mi parecer, todo valor.
segments.en: Many answered this sonnet, with differing opinions; among them the one I call the first of my friends replied, and he wrote then a sonnet which begins: You saw, I think, all worth.

segments.original: E questo fue quasi lo principio de l’amistà tra lui e me, quando elli seppe che io era quelli che li avea ciò mandato.
segments.es: Y esto fue casi el principio de la amistad entre él y yo, cuando supo que yo era quien se lo había enviado.
segments.en: And this was almost the beginning of the friendship between him and me, when he learned that I was the one who had sent it to him.

segments.original: Lo verace giudicio del detto sogno non fue veduto allora per alcuno, ma ora è manifestissimo a li più semplici.
segments.es: El verdadero sentido de aquel sueño no lo vio entonces nadie, pero ahora es clarísimo para los más sencillos.
segments.en: The true meaning of that dream was seen by no one then, but now it is plain to the simplest.

works.translation_credit: New AI working translation for Katabasis; not a published literary translation.

works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.title: So in my speech I want to be harsh
works.title_es: Así en mi hablar quiero ser áspero
works.scope: Rime, CIII · complete canzone, 83 lines
works.scope_es: Rime, CIII · canción completa, 83 versos
works.source_edition: Italian Wikisource, Rime (Dante), CIII. One transcription slip corrected: giungono for giuncono (line 12).
works.source_edition_es: Wikisource en italiano, Rime (Dante), CIII. Se corrige una errata de la transcripción: giungono por giuncono (verso 12).
works.note: One of the four “stony” poems for a woman Dante calls Petra, stone. The canzone asks for words as hard as she is, imagines Love striking the poet down, and ends by sending the song to wound her in return: fine honour is won in taking vengeance.
works.note_es: Uno de los cuatro poemas «pétreos» para una mujer a la que Dante llama Petra, piedra. La canción pide palabras tan duras como ella, imagina a Amor derribando al poeta y termina mandando el poema a herirla a ella: bella honra se gana al vengarse.

segments.original: Così nel mio parlar voglio esser aspro
segments.es: Así en mi hablar quiero ser áspero
segments.en: So in my speech I want to be harsh

segments.original: com’è ne li atti questa bella petra,
segments.es: como lo es en sus actos esta bella piedra,
segments.en: as this lovely stone is in her acts,

segments.original: la quale ognora impetra
segments.es: que a cada hora adquiere
segments.en: who hour by hour takes on

segments.original: maggior durezza e più natura cruda,
segments.es: mayor dureza y naturaleza más cruel,
segments.en: greater hardness and a crueller nature,

segments.original: e veste sua persona d’un diaspro
segments.es: y viste su persona de un jaspe
segments.en: and clothes her person in a jasper

segments.original: tal, che per lui, o perch’ella s’arretra,
segments.es: tal que, por él, o porque ella se retira,
segments.en: such that, through it, or because she draws back,

segments.original: non esce di faretra
segments.es: no sale de la aljaba
segments.en: there leaves no quiver

segments.original: saetta che già mai la colga ignuda:
segments.es: flecha que alguna vez la alcance desnuda:
segments.en: an arrow that will ever find her bare:

segments.original: ed ella ancide, e non val ch’om si chiuda
segments.es: y ella mata, y de nada sirve encerrarse
segments.en: and she kills, and it is no use to shut oneself away

segments.original: né si dilunghi da’ colpi mortali,
segments.es: ni alejarse de sus golpes mortales,
segments.en: or keep far from her mortal blows,

segments.original: che, com’avesser ali,
segments.es: que, como si tuvieran alas,
segments.en: which, as if they had wings,

segments.original: giungono altrui e spezzan ciascun’arme;
segments.es: alcanzan a cualquiera y rompen toda arma;
segments.en: overtake a man and shatter every weapon;

segments.original: sì ch’io non so da lei né posso atarme.
segments.es: de modo que ni sé ni puedo defenderme de ella.
segments.en: so that I neither know how nor am able to defend myself from her.

segments.original: Non trovo scudo ch’ella non mi spezzi
segments.es: No hallo escudo que ella no me rompa
segments.en: I find no shield that she does not break

segments.original: né loco che dal suo viso m’asconda;
segments.es: ni lugar que de su rostro me esconda;
segments.en: nor place that hides me from her face;

segments.original: ché, come fior di fronda,
segments.es: pues, como flor en la rama,
segments.en: for, like a flower on its bough,

segments.original: così de la mia mente tien la cima:
segments.es: así ocupa la cima de mi mente:
segments.en: so she holds the summit of my mind:

segments.original: cotanto del mio mal par che si prezzi,
segments.es: tanto parece importarle mi mal
segments.en: she seems to care as much for my pain

segments.original: quanto legno di mar che non lieva onda;
segments.es: como a un barco un mar que no levanta olas;
segments.en: as a ship cares for a sea that lifts no wave;

segments.original: e ’l peso che m’affonda
segments.es: y el peso que me hunde
segments.en: and the weight that sinks me

segments.original: è tal che non potrebbe adequar rima.
segments.es: es tal que ninguna rima podría igualarlo.
segments.en: is such that no rhyme could equal it.

segments.original: Ahi angosciosa e dispietata lima
segments.es: ¡Ay, lima angustiosa y despiadada
segments.en: Ah, anguished and pitiless file

segments.original: che sordamente la mia vita scemi,
segments.es: que sordamente vas mermando mi vida!,
segments.en: that silently wears my life away,

segments.original: perché non ti ritemi
segments.es: ¿por qué no temes
segments.en: why are you not afraid

segments.original: sì di rodermi il core a scorza a scorza,
segments.es: roerme el corazón capa a capa
segments.en: to gnaw my heart away layer by layer,

segments.original: com’io di dire altrui chi ti dà forza?
segments.es: como yo temo decir a otros quién te da fuerza?
segments.en: as I am afraid to tell others who gives you strength?

segments.original: Ché più mi triema il cor qualora io penso
segments.es: Pues más me tiembla el corazón cuando pienso
segments.en: For my heart trembles more whenever I think

segments.original: di lei in parte ov’altri li occhi induca,
segments.es: en ella donde otros puedan volver los ojos,
segments.en: of her where others might turn their eyes,

segments.original: per tema non traluca
segments.es: por temor de que se transparente
segments.en: for fear that it may shine through

segments.original: lo mio penser di fuor sì che si scopra,
segments.es: mi pensamiento por fuera y se descubra,
segments.en: my thought outwardly and be discovered,

segments.original: ch’io non fo de la morte, che ogni senso
segments.es: que ante la muerte, que cada sentido
segments.en: than it does at death, which is chewing

segments.original: co li denti d’Amor già mi manduca;
segments.es: con los dientes de Amor ya me mastica;
segments.en: every sense of mine already with Love’s teeth;

segments.original: ciò è che ’l pensier bruca
segments.es: es decir, que el pensamiento roe
segments.en: that is, my thought grazes away

segments.original: la lor vertù sì che n’allenta l’opra.
segments.es: su fuerza, y así afloja su obra.
segments.en: their strength, so that their work grows slack.

segments.original: E’ m’ha percosso in terra, e stammi sopra
segments.es: Me ha derribado en tierra, y está sobre mí
segments.en: He has struck me to the ground and stands over me

segments.original: con quella spada ond’elli ancise Dido,
segments.es: con aquella espada con que mató a Dido,
segments.en: with that sword with which he killed Dido,

segments.original: Amore, a cui io grido
segments.es: Amor, a quien grito
segments.en: Love, to whom I cry

segments.original: merzé chiamando, e umilmente il priego;
segments.es: clamando merced, y humildemente le ruego;
segments.en: calling for mercy, and humbly beg him;

segments.original: ed el d’ogni merzé par messo al niego.
segments.es: y él parece resuelto a negar toda merced.
segments.en: and he seems set on denying all mercy.

segments.original: Egli alza ad ora ad or la mano, e sfida
segments.es: Él alza una y otra vez la mano, y desafía
segments.en: Again and again he lifts his hand and challenges

segments.original: la debole mia vita, esto perverso,
segments.es: mi débil vida, este perverso,
segments.en: my feeble life, this perverse one,

segments.original: che disteso a riverso
segments.es: que, tendido boca arriba,
segments.en: who, laid out on my back,

segments.original: mi tiene in terra d’ogni guizzo stanco:
segments.es: me tiene en tierra, sin fuerzas para moverme:
segments.en: holds me on the ground, too spent to stir:

segments.original: allor mi surgon ne la mente strida;
segments.es: entonces me surgen gritos en la mente;
segments.en: then shrieks rise up in my mind;

segments.original: e ’l sangue, ch’è per le vene disperso,
segments.es: y la sangre, que por las venas está esparcida,
segments.en: and the blood that is scattered through my veins

segments.original: fuggendo corre verso
segments.es: huyendo corre hacia
segments.en: runs fleeing toward

segments.original: lo cor, che ’l chiama; ond’io rimango bianco.
segments.es: el corazón, que la llama; por eso quedo blanco.
segments.en: the heart, which calls it; so I am left white.

segments.original: Elli mi fiede sotto il braccio manco
segments.es: Me hiere bajo el brazo izquierdo
segments.en: He strikes me under the left arm

segments.original: sì forte, che ’l dolor nel cor rimbalza:
segments.es: tan fuerte que el dolor rebota en el corazón:
segments.en: so hard that the pain rebounds in my heart:

segments.original: allor dico: "S’elli alza
segments.es: entonces digo: «Si él alza
segments.en: then I say: “If he lifts

segments.original: un’altra volta, Morte m’avrà chiuso
segments.es: otra vez, la Muerte me habrá encerrado
segments.en: once more, Death will have shut me in

segments.original: prima che ’l colpo sia disceso giuso".
segments.es: antes de que el golpe haya caído».
segments.en: before the blow has fallen.”

segments.original: Così vedess’io lui fender per mezzo
segments.es: ¡Así lo viera yo partir por la mitad
segments.en: Would I could see him split in two

segments.original: lo core a la crudele che ’l mio squatra!
segments.es: el corazón de la cruel que descuartiza el mío!
segments.en: the heart of the cruel one who quarters mine!

segments.original: poi non mi sarebb’atra
segments.es: entonces no me sería negra
segments.en: then death would not be black to me,

segments.original: la morte, ov’io per sua bellezza corro:
segments.es: la muerte, hacia la que corro por su belleza:
segments.en: the death I run toward for her beauty:

segments.original: ché tanto dà nel sol quanto nel rezzo
segments.es: pues hiere tanto al sol como a la sombra
segments.en: for she strikes as much in sun as in shade,

segments.original: questa scherana micidiale e latra.
segments.es: esta salteadora asesina y ladrona.
segments.en: this murderous brigand and thief.

segments.original: Ohmè, perché non latra
segments.es: ¡Ay de mí!, ¿por qué no aúlla
segments.en: Alas, why does she not howl

segments.original: per me, com’io per lei, nel caldo borro?
segments.es: por mí, como yo por ella, en el barranco ardiente?
segments.en: for me, as I for her, in the burning gully?

segments.original: ché tosto griderei: "Io vi soccorro".
segments.es: pues pronto gritaría: «Yo os socorro».
segments.en: for I would cry at once: “I will help you.”

segments.original: e fare’l volentier, sì come quelli
segments.es: y lo haría de buen grado, como quien
segments.en: and I would do it gladly, as one

segments.original: che ne’ biondi capelli
segments.es: en los cabellos rubios
segments.en: who in the golden hair

segments.original: ch’Amor per consumarmi increspa e dora
segments.es: que Amor, para consumirme, riza y dora
segments.en: that Love curls and gilds to consume me

segments.original: metterei mano, e piacere’le allora.
segments.es: metería la mano, y entonces le agradaría.
segments.en: would lay my hand, and then she would like me.

segments.original: S’io avessi le belle trecce prese,
segments.es: Si yo hubiera tomado las bellas trenzas
segments.en: If I had seized the lovely tresses

segments.original: che fatte son per me scudiscio e ferza,
segments.es: que se han vuelto para mí fusta y látigo,
segments.en: that have become my whip and lash,

segments.original: pigliandole anzi terza,
segments.es: agarrándolas antes de tercia,
segments.en: taking hold of them before the third hour,

segments.original: con esse passerei vespero e squille:
segments.es: con ellas pasaría las vísperas y las campanas de la noche:
segments.en: with them I would pass vespers and the evening bells:

segments.original: e non sarei pietoso né cortese,
segments.es: y no sería piadoso ni cortés,
segments.en: and I would be neither merciful nor courteous,

segments.original: anzi farei com’orso quando scherza;
segments.es: sino que haría como el oso cuando juega;
segments.en: but would do as a bear does when it plays;

segments.original: e se Amor me ne sferza,
segments.es: y si Amor con ellas me azota,
segments.en: and if Love lashes me with them,

segments.original: io mi vendicherei di più di mille.
segments.es: me vengaría más de mil veces.
segments.en: I would take vengeance more than a thousandfold.

segments.original: Ancor ne li occhi, ond’escon le faville
segments.es: Y aun en los ojos, de donde salen las chispas
segments.en: Still into the eyes, from which the sparks come

segments.original: che m’infiammano il cor, ch’io porto anciso,
segments.es: que me inflaman el corazón, que llevo muerto,
segments.en: that set my heart on fire, which I carry slain,

segments.original: guarderei presso e fiso,
segments.es: miraría de cerca y fijamente,
segments.en: I would gaze close and fixed,

segments.original: per vendicar lo fuggir che mi face;
segments.es: para vengar su huida de mí;
segments.en: to avenge the way she flees from me;

segments.original: e poi le renderei con amor pace.
segments.es: y después le devolvería la paz con amor.
segments.en: and then with love I would give her back peace.

segments.original: Canzon, vattene dritto a quella donna
segments.es: Canción, vete derecha a aquella dama
segments.en: Song, go straight to that lady

segments.original: che m’ha ferito il core e che m’invola
segments.es: que me ha herido el corazón y me roba
segments.en: who has wounded my heart and who steals from me

segments.original: quello ond’io ho più gola,
segments.es: aquello de lo que tengo más hambre,
segments.en: what I hunger for most,

segments.original: e dàlle per lo cor d’una saetta;
segments.es: y clávale una flecha en el corazón;
segments.en: and strike her through the heart with an arrow;

segments.original: ché bell’onor s’acquista in far vendetta.
segments.es: pues bella honra se gana al vengarse.
segments.en: for fine honour is won in taking vengeance.

works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.title: The poets of arms, love and rectitude
works.title_es: Los poetas de las armas, del amor y de la rectitud
works.scope: De vulgari eloquentia, II.ii · from the three great subjects to the end of the chapter
works.scope_es: De vulgari eloquentia, II.ii · desde los tres grandes temas hasta el final del capítulo
works.source_edition: Dante Alighieri, De vulgari eloquentia, ed. Giovanni Battista Giuliani, Opere latine, vol. I (Florence, Le Monnier, 1878), Latin Wikisource. The Occitan and Italian lines Dante quotes are kept as printed.
works.source_edition_es: Dante Alighieri, De vulgari eloquentia, ed. de Giovanni Battista Giuliani, Opere latine, tomo I (Florencia, Le Monnier, 1878), Wikisource en latín. Los versos occitanos e italianos que cita Dante se conservan como están impresos.
works.note: Dante asks which subjects deserve the noblest vernacular and names three: arms, love and virtue. For arms his example is Bertran de Born, the troubadour lord of Hautefort; no Italian, he says, has yet sung of arms. The friend of Cino who sings rectitude is Dante himself.
works.note_es: Dante se pregunta qué temas merecen la lengua vulgar más noble y nombra tres: las armas, el amor y la virtud. Para las armas su ejemplo es Bertran de Born, el trovador señor de Autafòrt; ningún italiano, dice, ha cantado todavía las armas. El amigo de Cino que canta la rectitud es el propio Dante.

segments.original: Nunc autem quæ sint ipsa venemur.
segments.es: Ahora busquemos cuáles son esos temas.
segments.en: Now let us hunt out what those subjects are.

segments.original: Ad quorum evidentiam sciendum est, quod sicut homo tripliciter spirituatus est, videlicet vegetabilis, animalis et rationalis, triplex iter perambulat.
segments.es: Para verlo con claridad hay que saber que, así como el hombre tiene un alma de tres clases, vegetativa, animal y racional, recorre un triple camino.
segments.en: To make them plain, one must know that, as man has a threefold soul, vegetative, animal and rational, so he walks a threefold path.

segments.original: Nam secundum quod vegetabilis est, utile quærit, in quo cum plantis communicat; secundum quod animalis, delectabile, in quo cum brutis; secundum quod rationalis, honestum quærit, in quo solus est, vel Angelicæ naturæ sociatur.
segments.es: Pues en cuanto vegetativo busca lo útil, en lo que se asemeja a las plantas; en cuanto animal, lo placentero, en lo que se asemeja a las bestias; en cuanto racional, busca lo honesto, en lo que está solo o se une a la naturaleza de los ángeles.
segments.en: For as vegetative he seeks the useful, in which he shares with plants; as animal, the pleasurable, in which he shares with beasts; as rational, he seeks the honourable, in which he stands alone or is joined to the nature of the angels.

segments.original: Per hæc tria quicquid agimus, agere videmur; et quia in quolibet istorum quædam sunt majora, quædam maxima, secundum quod talia, quæ maxima sunt, maxime pertractanda videntur; et per consequens maximo Vulgari.
segments.es: Todo lo que hacemos parece que lo hacemos por estas tres cosas; y como en cada una hay cosas mayores y otras máximas, las máximas parecen las que más deben tratarse, y por tanto en la lengua vulgar más alta.
segments.en: Whatever we do, we seem to do for these three; and since in each some things are greater and some greatest, the greatest seem most to deserve treatment, and therefore in the highest vernacular.

segments.original: Sed disserendum est, quæ maxima sint; et primo in eo quod est utile: in quo, si callide consideremus intentum omnium quærentium utilitatem, nil aliud, quam Salutem inveniemus.
segments.es: Pero hay que examinar cuáles son las máximas. Primero en lo útil: si consideramos con agudeza lo que buscan todos los que buscan utilidad, no hallaremos otra cosa que la Salud.
segments.en: But we must discuss which are the greatest. First in the useful: if we shrewdly consider what all who seek advantage are aiming at, we shall find nothing but Safety.

segments.original: Secundo in eo, quod est delectabile: in quo dicimus illud esse maxime delectabile, quod per pretiosissimum objectum appetitus delectat: hoc autem Venus est.
segments.es: Segundo, en lo placentero: decimos que lo más placentero es lo que deleita por el objeto más precioso del deseo, y eso es Venus.
segments.en: Second, in the pleasurable: we say that most pleasurable is what delights through the most precious object of desire, and that is Venus.

segments.original: Tertio in eo, quod est honestum: in quo nemo dubitat esse Virtutem.
segments.es: Tercero, en lo honesto: nadie duda de que ahí está la Virtud.
segments.en: Third, in the honourable: no one doubts that Virtue lies there.

segments.original: Quare hæc tria, Salus videlicet, Venus, Virtus apparent esse illa magnalia, quæ sint maxime pertractanda, hoc est ea, quæ maxima sunt ad ista, ut armorum Probitas, amoris Accensio, et Directio voluntatis.
segments.es: Por eso estas tres, Salud, Venus y Virtud, aparecen como los grandes asuntos que más deben tratarse, es decir, lo máximo en ellas: la proeza de las armas, el ardor del amor y la rectitud de la voluntad.
segments.en: So these three, Safety, Venus and Virtue, appear to be the great matters most worth treating, that is, what is greatest in each: prowess in arms, the kindling of love, and the right direction of the will.

segments.original: Circa quæ sola, si bene recolimus, illustres viros invenimus vulgariter poetasse; scilicet Bertramum de Bornio, Arma; Arnaldum Danielem, Amorem; Gerardum de Bornello, Rectitudinem; Cinum Pistoriensem, Amorem; Amicum ejus, Rectitudinem.
segments.es: Solo sobre ellas, si recordamos bien, hallamos que los hombres ilustres han escrito poesía en lengua vulgar: Bertran de Born, las armas; Arnaut Daniel, el amor; Giraut de Bornelh, la rectitud; Cino da Pistoia, el amor; su amigo, la rectitud.
segments.en: On these alone, if we remember rightly, we find illustrious men have written poetry in the vernacular: Bertran de Born on arms; Arnaut Daniel on love; Giraut de Bornelh on rectitude; Cino da Pistoia on love; his friend on rectitude.

segments.original: Bertramus etenim ait:
segments.es: Pues Bertran dice:
segments.en: For Bertran says:

segments.original: «Non puesc mudar qu’un chantar non esparja.»
segments.es: «No puedo dejar de esparcir un canto.»
segments.en: “I cannot keep from spreading a song.”

segments.original: Arnaldus:
segments.es: Arnaut:
segments.en: Arnaut:

segments.original: «L’aura amara fa ’ls broils blancutz clarzir.»
segments.es: «El aire amargo aclara los sotos frondosos.»
segments.en: “The bitter wind thins out the leafy thickets.”

segments.original: Gerardus:
segments.es: Giraut:
segments.en: Giraut:

segments.original: «Per solatz revelhar
segments.es: «Para despertar la alegría
segments.en: “To wake up the delight

segments.original: Que s’es trop endormitz.»
segments.es: que se ha dormido demasiado.»
segments.en: that has slept too long.”

segments.original: Cinus:
segments.es: Cino:
segments.en: Cino:

segments.original: «Degno son io ch’io mora.»
segments.es: «Merezco morir.»
segments.en: “I deserve to die.”

segments.original: Amicus ejus
segments.es: Su amigo:
segments.en: His friend:

segments.original: «Doglia mi reca nello core ardire.»
segments.es: «El dolor me trae audacia al corazón.»
segments.en: “Grief brings boldness to my heart.”

segments.original: Arma vero nullum Italum adhuc invenio poetasse.
segments.es: Pero de las armas no encuentro todavía a ningún italiano que haya escrito poesía.
segments.en: But on arms I find no Italian who has yet written poetry.

segments.original: His proinde visis, quæ canenda sint Vulgari altissimo innotescunt.
segments.es: Visto esto, queda claro qué debe cantarse en la lengua vulgar más alta.
segments.en: With this seen, it becomes clear what must be sung in the highest vernacular.

works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.title: Riches and the generosity of Bertran de Born
works.title_es: Las riquezas y la generosidad de Bertran de Born
works.scope: Convivio, IV.xi, 6–14 · to the end of the chapter
works.scope_es: Convivio, IV.xi, 6–14 · hasta el final del capítulo
works.source_edition: Italian Wikisource, Convivio, Trattato quarto, chapter XI. Paragraph numbers and the editorial square brackets around restored letters removed (cui, nel, liberalitade).
works.source_edition_es: Wikisource en italiano, Convivio, Trattato quarto, capítulo XI. Se quitan los números de párrafo y los corchetes editoriales de las letras restituidas (cui, nel, liberalitade).
works.note: Dante argues that riches reach the wicked more often than the good, and that their only good use is to be given away: a gift buys hearts. Among the generous whom everyone still remembers he names Bertran de Born. “The Provençal” of the wish is a troubadour whose name Dante does not give.
works.note_es: Dante sostiene que las riquezas llegan más a los malvados que a los buenos, y que su único buen uso es darlas: un regalo compra corazones. Entre los generosos que todos recuerdan nombra a Bertran de Born. «El provenzal» del deseo es un trovador cuyo nombre Dante no da.

segments.original: Dico che la loro imperfezione primamente si può notare ne la indiscrezione del loro avvenimento, nel quale nulla distributiva giustizia risplende, ma tutta iniquitade quasi sempre, la quale iniquitade è proprio effetto d’imperfezione.
segments.es: Digo que la imperfección de las riquezas se puede ver primero en lo indiscriminado de su llegada, en la que no brilla ninguna justicia distributiva, sino casi siempre pura iniquidad, y esa iniquidad es efecto propio de la imperfección.
segments.en: I say that the imperfection of riches can be seen first in the indiscriminate way they arrive, in which no distributive justice shines, but almost always sheer iniquity, and that iniquity is the proper effect of imperfection.

segments.original: Che se si considerano li modi per li quali esse vegnono, tutti si possono in tre maniere ricogliere:
segments.es: Porque si se consideran los modos por los que llegan, todos se pueden reunir en tres maneras:
segments.en: For if we consider the ways by which they come, all can be gathered into three:

segments.original: chè o vengono da pura fortuna, sì come quando sanza intenzione o speranza vegnono per invenzione alcuna non pensata;
segments.es: o vienen de pura fortuna, como cuando llegan sin intención ni esperanza por algún hallazgo impensado;
segments.en: either they come from pure fortune, as when they arrive without intention or hope through some unlooked-for find;

segments.original: o vengono da fortuna che è da ragione aiutata, sì come per testamenti o per mutua successione;
segments.es: o vienen de una fortuna ayudada por la razón, como por testamento o por sucesión;
segments.en: or they come from fortune helped by reason, as by wills or by succession;

segments.original: o vegnono da fortuna aiutatrice di ragione, sì come quando per licito o per illicito procaccio: licito dico, quando è per arte o per mercatantia o per servigio meritante; illicito dico, quando è per furto o per rapina.
segments.es: o vienen de una fortuna que ayuda a la razón, como cuando se obtienen por ganancia lícita o ilícita: lícita, digo, cuando es por un oficio, por el comercio o por un servicio que lo merece; ilícita, cuando es por hurto o por rapiña.
segments.en: or they come from fortune that helps reason, as when they are gained by lawful or unlawful means: lawful, I mean, when by a craft, by trade, or by deserving service; unlawful, when by theft or robbery.

segments.original: E in ciascuno di questi tre modi si vede quella iniquitade che io dico, chè più volte a li malvagi che a li buoni le celate ricchezze che si truovano o che si ritruovano si rappresentano; e questo è sì manifesto, che non ha mestiere di pruova.
segments.es: Y en cada uno de estos tres modos se ve la iniquidad que digo, pues las riquezas escondidas que se encuentran o se recuperan aparecen más veces ante los malvados que ante los buenos; y esto es tan evidente que no necesita prueba.
segments.en: And in each of these three ways one sees the iniquity I speak of, for hidden riches that are found or found again turn up more often to the wicked than to the good; and this is so plain that it needs no proof.

segments.original: Veramente io vidi lo luogo, ne le coste d’un monte che si chiama Falterona, in Toscana, dove lo più vile villano di tutta la contrada, zappando, più d’uno staio di santalene d’argento finissimo vi trovò, che forse più di dumilia anni l’aveano aspettato.
segments.es: En verdad yo vi el lugar, en las laderas de un monte que se llama Falterona, en Toscana, donde el más vil de los labriegos de toda la comarca, cavando, encontró más de una fanega de monedas antiguas de plata finísima, que quizá lo habían esperado más de dos mil años.
segments.en: Indeed I saw the place, on the slopes of a mountain called Falterona in Tuscany, where the basest peasant in the whole district, while hoeing, found more than a bushel of ancient coins of the finest silver, which had perhaps been waiting for him more than two thousand years.

segments.original: E per vedere questa iniquitade, disse Aristotile che «quanto l’uomo più subiace a lo ’ntelletto, tanto meno subiace a la fortuna».
segments.es: Y viendo esta iniquidad dijo Aristóteles que «cuanto más se somete el hombre al intelecto, tanto menos se somete a la fortuna».
segments.en: And seeing this iniquity, Aristotle said that “the more a man is subject to the intellect, the less he is subject to fortune.”

segments.original: E dico che più volte a li malvagi che a li buoni pervengono li retaggi, legati e caduti; e di ciò non voglio recare innanzi alcuna testimonianza, ma ciascuno volga li occhi per la sua vicinanza, e vedrà quello che io mi taccio per non abominare alcuno.
segments.es: Y digo que las herencias, los legados y los bienes vacantes llegan más veces a los malvados que a los buenos; y de ello no quiero aducir ningún testimonio, sino que cada cual mire a su alrededor, en su vecindad, y verá lo que yo callo por no afrentar a nadie.
segments.en: And I say that inheritances, legacies and escheats come more often to the wicked than to the good; and of this I will bring no witness, but let each man look around his own neighbourhood, and he will see what I keep silent so as to shame no one.

segments.original: Così fosse piaciuto a Dio che quello che addomandò lo Provenzale fosse stato, che chi non è reda de la bontade perdesse lo retaggio de l’avere!
segments.es: ¡Ojalá hubiera querido Dios que se cumpliera lo que pidió el provenzal: que quien no es heredero de la bondad perdiera la herencia de los bienes!
segments.en: Would it had pleased God that what the Provençal asked for had come to pass: that whoever is not heir to goodness should lose the inheritance of wealth!

segments.original: E dico che più volte a li malvagi che a li buoni pervegnono a punto li procacci; chè li non liciti a li buoni mai non pervegnono, però che li rifiutano.
segments.es: Y digo que también las ganancias llegan más veces a los malvados que a los buenos; pues las ilícitas nunca llegan a los buenos, porque las rechazan.
segments.en: And I say that gains, too, come more often to the wicked than to the good; for unlawful ones never come to the good, since they refuse them.

segments.original: E quale buono uomo mai per forza o per fraude procaccerà? Impossibile sarebbe ciò, chè solo per la elezione de la illicita impresa più buono non sarebbe.
segments.es: ¿Y qué hombre bueno buscará jamás ganancia por la fuerza o por el fraude? Sería imposible, pues con solo elegir la empresa ilícita ya no sería bueno.
segments.en: And what good man will ever seek gain by force or fraud? It would be impossible, for merely by choosing the unlawful undertaking he would no longer be good.

segments.original: E li liciti rade volte pervegnono a li buoni, perchè, con ciò sia cosa che molta sollicitudine quivi si richeggia, e la sollicitudine del buono sia diritta a maggiori cose, rade volte sofficientemente quivi lo buono è sollicito.
segments.es: Y las lícitas rara vez llegan a los buenos, porque, como allí se requiere mucha diligencia y la diligencia del bueno se dirige a cosas mayores, rara vez el bueno pone allí suficiente empeño.
segments.en: And lawful ones rarely come to the good, because, since much diligence is needed there and the good man’s diligence is turned to greater things, he is rarely diligent enough there.

segments.original: Per che è manifesto in ciascuno modo quelle ricchezze iniquamente avvenire; e però Nostro Segnore inique le chiamò, quando disse: «Fatevi amici de la pecunia de la iniquitade», invitando e confortando li uomini a liberalitade di benefici, che sono generatori d’amici.
segments.es: Por eso es manifiesto que, de cualquier modo, esas riquezas llegan inicuamente; y por eso Nuestro Señor las llamó inicuas cuando dijo: «Haceos amigos con el dinero de la iniquidad», invitando y animando a los hombres a la liberalidad de los beneficios, que engendran amigos.
segments.en: So it is plain that in every way those riches arrive unjustly; and therefore Our Lord called them unrighteous when he said, “Make friends for yourselves with the mammon of unrighteousness,” inviting and urging men to generous giving, which begets friends.

segments.original: E quanto fa bello cambio chi di queste imperfettissime cose dà per avere e per acquistare cose perfette, sì come li cuori de’ valenti uomini! Lo cambio ogni die si può fare.
segments.es: ¡Y qué hermoso cambio hace quien da de estas cosas imperfectísimas para tener y adquirir cosas perfectas, como los corazones de los hombres valiosos! Ese cambio puede hacerse cada día.
segments.en: And what a fine exchange he makes who gives of these most imperfect things to have and win perfect ones, such as the hearts of worthy men! The exchange can be made every day.

segments.original: Certo nuova mercatantia è questa de l’altre, che, credendo comperare uno uomo per lo beneficio, mille e mille ne sono comperati.
segments.es: Ciertamente este comercio es distinto de todos los demás, pues creyendo comprar a un hombre con el beneficio, se compran miles y miles.
segments.en: Surely this trade is unlike all others, for, thinking to buy one man with a kindness, one buys thousands upon thousands.

segments.original: E cui non è ancora nel cuore Alessandro per li suoi reali benefici? Cui non è ancora lo buono re di Castella, o il Saladino, o il buono Marchese di Monferrato, o il buono Conte di Tolosa, o Beltramo dal Bornio, o Galasso di Montefeltro?
segments.es: ¿Y en el corazón de quién no vive todavía Alejandro por sus regios beneficios? ¿En el de quién no viven todavía el buen rey de Castilla, o Saladino, o el buen marqués de Monferrato, o el buen conde de Tolosa, o Bertran de Born, o Galasso da Montefeltro?
segments.en: And in whose heart does Alexander not still live for his royal gifts? In whose do not still live the good king of Castile, or Saladin, or the good Marquis of Montferrat, or the good Count of Toulouse, or Bertran de Born, or Galasso of Montefeltro?

segments.original: Quando de le loro messioni si fa menzione, certo non solamente quelli che ciò farebbero volentieri, ma quelli prima morire vorrebbero che ciò fare, amore hanno a la memoria di costoro.
segments.es: Cuando se mencionan sus dádivas, no solo quienes harían lo mismo de buen grado, sino incluso quienes preferirían morir antes que hacerlo, sienten amor por la memoria de estos hombres.
segments.en: When their largesse is mentioned, not only those who would gladly do the same, but even those who would rather die than do it, cherish the memory of these men.

works.author: Dante Alighieri
works.title: Letter to a Florentine friend
works.scope: Epistola XII · complete letter
works.scope_es: Epistola XII · carta completa
works.source_edition: Latin Wikisource, Epistulae (Dantes Aligherius), XII. Paragraph numbers removed; spacing before question marks normalised.
works.source_edition_es: Wikisource en latín, Epistulae (Dantes Aligherius), XII. Se quitan los números de párrafo y se normaliza el espacio ante los signos de interrogación.
works.note: In 1315 Florence offered its exiles a pardon if they paid a fine and walked as penitents to be offered at the Baptistery, the “offering” of the letter. Dante, banished since 1302, answers a friend who had written to him about it. Ciolo is a Florentine who had accepted those terms.
works.note_es: En 1315 Florencia ofreció el perdón a sus desterrados si pagaban una multa y se presentaban como penitentes para ser ofrecidos en el Baptisterio: la «oblación» de la carta. Dante, desterrado desde 1302, responde a un amigo que le había escrito sobre ello. Ciolo es un florentino que había aceptado esas condiciones.

segments.original: In litteris vestris et reverentia debita et affectione receptis, quam repatriatio mea cure sit vobis et animo, grata mente ac diligenti animadversione concepi;
segments.es: En vuestra carta, recibida con la debida reverencia y con afecto, he comprendido con ánimo agradecido y atenta consideración cuánto os ocupa y preocupa mi regreso a la patria;
segments.en: In your letter, received with due reverence and affection, I have understood with a grateful mind and careful attention how much my return home weighs on your care and your heart;

segments.original: et inde tanto me districtius obligastis, quanto rarius exules invenire amicos contingit.
segments.es: y con ello me habéis obligado tanto más estrechamente cuanto más raro es que los desterrados encuentren amigos.
segments.en: and by this you have bound me all the more closely, the more rarely it happens that exiles find friends.

segments.original: Ad illarum vero significata responsio, etsi non erit qualem forsan pusillanimitas appeteret aliquorum, ut suo examine vestri consilii ante iudicium ventiletur, affectuose deposco.
segments.es: En cuanto a mi respuesta a lo que en ella se me dice, aunque no sea la que quizá desearía la pusilanimidad de algunos, os ruego con afecto que la examinéis con vuestro buen juicio antes de juzgarla.
segments.en: As for my answer to what it tells me, though it may not be what the faint-heartedness of some would wish, I affectionately beg that it be weighed by your counsel before judgement is passed.

segments.original: Ecce igitur quod per litteras vestras meique nepotis nec non aliorum quamplurium amicorum, significatum est michi per ordinamentum nuper factum Florentie super absolutione bannitorum quod si solvere vellem certam pecunie quantitatem vellemque pati notam oblationis, et absolvi possem et redire ad presens.
segments.es: Pues bien, por vuestra carta y por las de mi sobrino y de otros muchos amigos se me ha hecho saber que, según una ordenanza dictada hace poco en Florencia sobre el perdón de los desterrados, si yo quisiera pagar cierta cantidad de dinero y aceptara la afrenta de la oblación, podría ser absuelto y volver ahora mismo.
segments.en: Here, then, is what your letter, and my nephew’s, and those of many other friends have made known to me: under a decree lately passed in Florence on the pardon of exiles, if I were willing to pay a certain sum of money and to bear the brand of the offering, I could be pardoned and return at once.

segments.original: In qua quidem duo ridenda et male preconsiliata sunt, pater; dico male preconsiliata per illos qui talia expresserunt, nam vestre littere discretius et consultius clausulate nichil de talibus continebant.
segments.es: En ello hay dos cosas ridículas y mal pensadas, padre; mal pensadas, digo, por quienes las expresaron, pues vuestra carta, escrita con más discreción y prudencia, no contenía nada de eso.
segments.en: In this there are two things laughable and ill-advised, father; ill-advised, I mean, by those who put them into words, for your letter, more discreetly and prudently phrased, contained nothing of the kind.

segments.original: Estne ista revocatio gratiosa qua Dantes Alagherii revocatur ad patriam, per trilustrium fere perpessus exilium?
segments.es: ¿Es esta la llamada generosa con que Dante Alighieri es llamado de vuelta a su patria, tras sufrir casi quince años de destierro?
segments.en: Is this the gracious recall by which Dante Alighieri is summoned back to his homeland, after enduring almost fifteen years of exile?

segments.original: Hocne meruit innocentia manifesta quibuslibet? hoc sudor et labor continuatus in studio?
segments.es: ¿Esto ha merecido una inocencia manifiesta a todos? ¿Esto, el sudor y el trabajo incesante del estudio?
segments.en: Is this what an innocence plain to all has earned? This, the sweat and unbroken toil of study?

segments.original: Absit a viro phylosophie domestico temeraria tantum cordis humilitas, ut more cuiusdam Cioli et aliorum infamium quasi vinctus ipse se patiatur offerri!
segments.es: ¡Lejos de un hombre familiar de la filosofía una humildad de corazón tan temeraria que, como un tal Ciolo y otros infames, se deje ofrecer como si estuviera encadenado!
segments.en: Far be it from a man at home with philosophy to show such reckless lowliness of heart as to let himself be offered up, like a certain Ciolo and other infamous men, as if in chains!

segments.original: Absit a viro predicante iustitiam ut perpessus iniurias, iniuriam inferentibus, velut benemerentibus, pecuniam suam solvat!
segments.es: ¡Lejos de un hombre que predica la justicia que, habiendo sufrido injurias, pague su dinero a quienes lo injuriaron, como si lo merecieran!
segments.en: Far be it from a man who preaches justice that, having suffered wrongs, he should pay his money to those who wronged him, as though they deserved it!

segments.original: Non est hec via redeundi ad patriam, pater mi;
segments.es: No es este el camino para volver a la patria, padre mío;
segments.en: This is not the way to return to my homeland, my father;

segments.original: sed si alia per vos ante aut deinde per alios invenitur que fame Dantisque honori non deroget, illam non lentis passibus acceptabo;
segments.es: pero si vos primero, u otros después, encontráis otro que no menoscabe la fama y el honor de Dante, lo tomaré con pasos nada lentos;
segments.en: but if another is found, by you first or later by others, that does not detract from Dante’s fame and honour, I will take it with no slow steps;

segments.original: quod si per nullam talem Florentia introitur, nunquam Florentiam introibo.
segments.es: y si por ninguno así se entra en Florencia, nunca entraré en Florencia.
segments.en: and if Florence is entered by no such way, I shall never enter Florence.

segments.original: Quidni? nonne solis astrorumque specula ubique conspiciam?
segments.es: ¿Y por qué no? ¿Acaso no podré contemplar en todas partes el espejo del sol y de los astros?
segments.en: Why not? Shall I not behold the mirror of the sun and stars everywhere?

segments.original: nonne dulcissimas veritates potero speculari ubique suo celo, ni prius inglorium ymo ignominiosum populo Florentineque civitati me reddam?
segments.es: ¿Acaso no podré meditar en todas partes, bajo el cielo, las verdades más dulces sin antes volverme sin gloria, más aún, ignominioso, ante el pueblo y la ciudad de Florencia?
segments.en: Shall I not be able to contemplate the sweetest truths anywhere under heaven, without first rendering myself inglorious, nay ignominious, before the people and city of Florence?

segments.original: Quippe nec panis deficiet.
segments.es: Y pan, por cierto, no me faltará.
segments.en: And bread, surely, will not fail me.

works.note: Huck has helped Jim, who fled slavery, travel down the Mississippi on a raft. Now Jim has been caught and is held for a reward, and Huck’s conscience, formed by the slaveholding world he grew up in, tells him that turning Jim in is right. The novel keeps that world’s racial slur in Huck’s mouth.
works.note_es: Huck ha ayudado a Jim, que huyó de la esclavitud, a bajar el Misisipi en una balsa. Ahora Jim ha sido capturado y lo retienen por una recompensa, y la conciencia de Huck, formada en el mundo esclavista donde creció, le dice que entregarlo es lo correcto. La novela mantiene en boca de Huck el insulto racial de ese mundo.

segments.original: It made me shiver.
segments.es: Me hizo temblar.
segments.en: It made me shiver.

segments.original: And I about made up my mind to pray, and see if I couldn’t try to quit being the kind of a boy I was and be better.
segments.es: Y casi decidí rezar, a ver si podía dejar de ser la clase de muchacho que era y ser mejor.
segments.en: And I about made up my mind to pray, and see if I couldn’t try to quit being the kind of a boy I was and be better.

segments.original: So I kneeled down. But the words wouldn’t come.
segments.es: Así que me arrodillé. Pero las palabras no salían.
segments.en: So I kneeled down. But the words wouldn’t come.

segments.original: Why wouldn’t they? It warn’t no use to try and hide it from Him. Nor from me, neither.
segments.es: ¿Por qué no salían? No servía de nada intentar ocultárselo a Él. Ni a mí tampoco.
segments.en: Why wouldn’t they? It warn’t no use to try and hide it from Him. Nor from me, neither.

segments.original: I knowed very well why they wouldn’t come. It was because my heart warn’t right; it was because I warn’t square; it was because I was playing double.
segments.es: Sabía muy bien por qué no salían. Era porque mi corazón no estaba limpio; porque yo no era honrado; porque estaba jugando a dos bandas.
segments.en: I knowed very well why they wouldn’t come. It was because my heart warn’t right; it was because I warn’t square; it was because I was playing double.

segments.original: I was letting on to give up sin, but away inside of me I was holding on to the biggest one of all.
segments.es: Fingía que dejaba el pecado, pero muy adentro me aferraba al más grande de todos.
segments.en: I was letting on to give up sin, but away inside of me I was holding on to the biggest one of all.

segments.original: I was trying to make my mouth say I would do the right thing and the clean thing, and go and write to that nigger’s owner and tell where he was; but deep down in me I knowed it was a lie, and He knowed it.
segments.es: Intentaba que mi boca dijera que haría lo correcto y lo limpio, que iría a escribirle a la dueña de ese negro para decirle dónde estaba; pero en el fondo sabía que era mentira, y Él lo sabía.
segments.en: I was trying to make my mouth say I would do the right thing and the clean thing, and go and write to that nigger’s owner and tell where he was; but deep down in me I knowed it was a lie, and He knowed it.

segments.original: You can’t pray a lie—I found that out.
segments.es: No se puede rezar una mentira: eso lo aprendí.
segments.en: You can’t pray a lie—I found that out.

segments.original: So I was full of trouble, full as I could be; and didn’t know what to do.
segments.es: Así que estaba lleno de angustia, todo lo lleno que se puede estar, y no sabía qué hacer.
segments.en: So I was full of trouble, full as I could be; and didn’t know what to do.

segments.original: At last I had an idea; and I says, I’ll go and write the letter—and then see if I can pray.
segments.es: Al fin tuve una idea, y me dije: voy a escribir la carta, y luego veré si puedo rezar.
segments.en: At last I had an idea; and I says, I’ll go and write the letter—and then see if I can pray.

segments.original: Why, it was astonishing, the way I felt as light as a feather right straight off, and my troubles all gone.
segments.es: Vaya, era asombroso: enseguida me sentí ligero como una pluma, y todas mis penas se habían ido.
segments.en: Why, it was astonishing, the way I felt as light as a feather right straight off, and my troubles all gone.

segments.original: So I got a piece of paper and a pencil, all glad and excited, and set down and wrote:
segments.es: Así que tomé un trozo de papel y un lápiz, contento y emocionado, me senté y escribí:
segments.en: So I got a piece of paper and a pencil, all glad and excited, and set down and wrote:

segments.original: Miss Watson, your runaway nigger Jim is down here two mile below Pikesville, and Mr. Phelps has got him and he will give him up for the reward if you send.
segments.es: Señorita Watson: su negro fugitivo Jim está aquí abajo, dos millas al sur de Pikesville, y el señor Phelps lo tiene y lo entregará por la recompensa si usted la manda.
segments.en: Miss Watson, your runaway nigger Jim is down here two mile below Pikesville, and Mr. Phelps has got him and he will give him up for the reward if you send.

segments.original: Huck Finn.
segments.es: Huck Finn.
segments.en: Huck Finn.

segments.original: I felt good and all washed clean of sin for the first time I had ever felt so in my life, and I knowed I could pray now.
segments.es: Me sentí bien, lavado y limpio de pecado por primera vez en mi vida, y supe que ahora sí podía rezar.
segments.en: I felt good and all washed clean of sin for the first time I had ever felt so in my life, and I knowed I could pray now.

segments.original: But I didn’t do it straight off, but laid the paper down and set there thinking—thinking how good it was all this happened so, and how near I come to being lost and going to hell.
segments.es: Pero no lo hice enseguida, sino que dejé el papel y me quedé allí sentado pensando: pensando en lo bueno que era que todo hubiera pasado así, y en lo cerca que había estado de perderme e ir al infierno.
segments.en: But I didn’t do it straight off, but laid the paper down and set there thinking—thinking how good it was all this happened so, and how near I come to being lost and going to hell.

segments.original: And went on thinking. And got to thinking over our trip down the river; and I see Jim before me all the time: in the day and in the night-time, sometimes moonlight, sometimes storms, and we a-floating along, talking and singing and laughing.
segments.es: Y seguí pensando. Y me puse a pensar en nuestro viaje río abajo; y veía a Jim delante de mí todo el tiempo: de día y de noche, a veces con luna, a veces con tormenta, y nosotros flotando, hablando, cantando y riendo.
segments.en: And went on thinking. And got to thinking over our trip down the river; and I see Jim before me all the time: in the day and in the night-time, sometimes moonlight, sometimes storms, and we a-floating along, talking and singing and laughing.

segments.original: But somehow I couldn’t seem to strike no places to harden me against him, but only the other kind.
segments.es: Pero no sé cómo, no daba con ningún recuerdo que me endureciera contra él, sino solo con los otros.
segments.en: But somehow I couldn’t seem to strike no places to harden me against him, but only the other kind.

segments.original: I’d see him standing my watch on top of his’n, ’stead of calling me, so I could go on sleeping; and see him how glad he was when I come back out of the fog;
segments.es: Lo veía haciendo mi guardia además de la suya, en vez de llamarme, para que yo pudiera seguir durmiendo; y veía lo contento que se puso cuando volví de la niebla;
segments.en: I’d see him standing my watch on top of his’n, ’stead of calling me, so I could go on sleeping; and see him how glad he was when I come back out of the fog;

segments.original: and when I come to him again in the swamp, up there where the feud was; and such-like times; and would always call me honey, and pet me and do everything he could think of for me, and how good he always was;
segments.es: y cuando lo volví a encontrar en el pantano, allá arriba, donde la guerra entre familias; y otras veces así; y siempre me llamaba cariño, y me mimaba y hacía por mí todo lo que se le ocurría, y lo bueno que era siempre;
segments.en: and when I come to him again in the swamp, up there where the feud was; and such-like times; and would always call me honey, and pet me and do everything he could think of for me, and how good he always was;

segments.original: and at last I struck the time I saved him by telling the men we had small-pox aboard, and he was so grateful, and said I was the best friend old Jim ever had in the world, and the only one he’s got now;
segments.es: y al fin di con la vez que lo salvé diciendo a los hombres que teníamos viruela a bordo, y él se puso tan agradecido, y dijo que yo era el mejor amigo que el viejo Jim había tenido en el mundo, y el único que tenía ahora;
segments.en: and at last I struck the time I saved him by telling the men we had small-pox aboard, and he was so grateful, and said I was the best friend old Jim ever had in the world, and the only one he’s got now;

segments.original: and then I happened to look around and see that paper.
segments.es: y entonces, por casualidad, miré alrededor y vi aquel papel.
segments.en: and then I happened to look around and see that paper.

segments.original: It was a close place. I took it up, and held it in my hand.
segments.es: Era un trance apurado. Lo recogí y lo sostuve en la mano.
segments.en: It was a close place. I took it up, and held it in my hand.

segments.original: I was a-trembling, because I’d got to decide, forever, betwixt two things, and I knowed it.
segments.es: Estaba temblando, porque tenía que decidir, para siempre, entre dos cosas, y lo sabía.
segments.en: I was a-trembling, because I’d got to decide, forever, betwixt two things, and I knowed it.

segments.original: I studied a minute, sort of holding my breath, and then says to myself:
segments.es: Lo pensé un minuto, como conteniendo el aliento, y luego me dije:
segments.en: I studied a minute, sort of holding my breath, and then says to myself:

segments.original: “All right, then, I’ll go to hell”—and tore it up.
segments.es: «Muy bien, entonces iré al infierno», y lo rompí.
segments.en: “All right, then, I’ll go to hell”—and tore it up.

segments.original: It was awful thoughts and awful words, but they was said. And I let them stay said; and never thought no more about reforming.
segments.es: Eran pensamientos terribles y palabras terribles, pero estaban dichas. Y las dejé dichas; y nunca más pensé en enmendarme.
segments.en: It was awful thoughts and awful words, but they was said. And I let them stay said; and never thought no more about reforming.

segments.original: I shoved the whole thing out of my head, and said I would take up wickedness again, which was in my line, being brung up to it, and the other warn’t.
segments.es: Me saqué todo aquello de la cabeza y dije que volvería a la maldad, que era lo mío, pues me habían criado en ella, y lo otro no.
segments.en: I shoved the whole thing out of my head, and said I would take up wickedness again, which was in my line, being brung up to it, and the other warn’t.

segments.original: And for a starter I would go to work and steal Jim out of slavery again; and if I could think up anything worse, I would do that, too; because as long as I was in, and in for good, I might as well go the whole hog.
segments.es: Y para empezar me pondría manos a la obra para robar otra vez a Jim de la esclavitud; y si se me ocurría algo peor, también lo haría; porque, ya que estaba metido, y metido para siempre, más valía llegar hasta el final.
segments.en: And for a starter I would go to work and steal Jim out of slavery again; and if I could think up anything worse, I would do that, too; because as long as I was in, and in for good, I might as well go the whole hog.
