works.author: Mark Twain
works.title: The boys’ ambition
works.scope: Life on the Mississippi, chapter IV · the first three paragraphs
works.scope_es: La vida en el Misisipi, capítulo IV · los tres primeros párrafos
works.source_edition: Mark Twain, Life on the Mississippi (1883), Project Gutenberg 245. The footnote naming the village (Hannibal, Missouri) is left out of the running text; double hyphens set as dashes; italics omitted.
works.source_edition_es: Mark Twain, Life on the Mississippi (1883), Project Gutenberg 245. La nota que nombra el pueblo (Hannibal, Misuri) queda fuera del texto; los guiones dobles se componen como rayas; se omiten las cursivas.
works.note: Twain grew up in Hannibal, Missouri, on the Mississippi, and was a steamboat pilot until the Civil War closed the river. The chapter remembers the town waiting all day for the packet boat.
works.note_es: Twain creció en Hannibal, Misuri, a orillas del Misisipi, y fue piloto de vapores hasta que la guerra civil cerró el río. El capítulo recuerda al pueblo esperando todo el día el vapor correo.

segments.original: When I was a boy, there was but one permanent ambition among my comrades in our village on the west bank of the Mississippi River. That was, to be a steamboatman.
segments.es: Cuando yo era niño, entre mis compañeros de nuestro pueblo, en la orilla occidental del río Misisipi, había una sola ambición permanente: trabajar en los vapores.
segments.en: When I was a boy, there was but one permanent ambition among my comrades in our village on the west bank of the Mississippi River. That was, to be a steamboatman.

segments.original: We had transient ambitions of other sorts, but they were only transient.
segments.es: Teníamos ambiciones pasajeras de otras clases, pero solo eran pasajeras.
segments.en: We had transient ambitions of other sorts, but they were only transient.

segments.original: When a circus came and went, it left us all burning to become clowns; the first negro minstrel show that came to our section left us all suffering to try that kind of life; now and then we had a hope that if we lived and were good, God would permit us to be pirates.
segments.es: Cuando un circo venía y se iba, nos dejaba a todos ardiendo por ser payasos; el primer espectáculo de minstrels negros que llegó a nuestra comarca nos dejó a todos sufriendo por probar esa vida; de vez en cuando teníamos la esperanza de que, si vivíamos y éramos buenos, Dios nos permitiría ser piratas.
segments.en: When a circus came and went, it left us all burning to become clowns; the first negro minstrel show that came to our section left us all suffering to try that kind of life; now and then we had a hope that if we lived and were good, God would permit us to be pirates.

segments.original: These ambitions faded out, each in its turn; but the ambition to be a steamboatman always remained.
segments.es: Esas ambiciones se desvanecían, cada una a su turno; pero la de trabajar en los vapores permanecía siempre.
segments.en: These ambitions faded out, each in its turn; but the ambition to be a steamboatman always remained.

segments.original: Once a day a cheap, gaudy packet arrived upward from St. Louis, and another downward from Keokuk.
segments.es: Una vez al día llegaba río arriba un vapor barato y chillón desde San Luis, y otro río abajo desde Keokuk.
segments.en: Once a day a cheap, gaudy packet arrived upward from St. Louis, and another downward from Keokuk.

segments.original: Before these events, the day was glorious with expectancy; after them, the day was a dead and empty thing. Not only the boys, but the whole village, felt this.
segments.es: Antes de esos acontecimientos, el día era glorioso de expectación; después, el día era una cosa muerta y vacía. No solo los muchachos, sino todo el pueblo, lo sentía así.
segments.en: Before these events, the day was glorious with expectancy; after them, the day was a dead and empty thing. Not only the boys, but the whole village, felt this.

segments.original: After all these years I can picture that old time to myself now, just as it was then:
segments.es: Después de todos estos años puedo imaginar aquel tiempo tal como era entonces:
segments.en: After all these years I can picture that old time to myself now, just as it was then:

segments.original: the white town drowsing in the sunshine of a summer's morning; the streets empty, or pretty nearly so;
segments.es: el pueblo blanco adormilado al sol de una mañana de verano; las calles vacías, o casi;
segments.en: the white town drowsing in the sunshine of a summer's morning; the streets empty, or pretty nearly so;

segments.original: one or two clerks sitting in front of the Water Street stores, with their splint-bottomed chairs tilted back against the wall, chins on breasts, hats slouched over their faces, asleep—with shingle-shavings enough around to show what broke them down;
segments.es: uno o dos dependientes sentados frente a las tiendas de Water Street, con sus sillas de asiento de tiras de madera inclinadas contra la pared, la barbilla en el pecho, el sombrero caído sobre la cara, dormidos, con virutas alrededor que mostraban qué los había rendido;
segments.en: one or two clerks sitting in front of the Water Street stores, with their splint-bottomed chairs tilted back against the wall, chins on breasts, hats slouched over their faces, asleep—with shingle-shavings enough around to show what broke them down;

segments.original: a sow and a litter of pigs loafing along the sidewalk, doing a good business in watermelon rinds and seeds;
segments.es: una cerda y su camada holgazaneando por la acera, haciendo buen negocio con cáscaras y pepitas de sandía;
segments.en: a sow and a litter of pigs loafing along the sidewalk, doing a good business in watermelon rinds and seeds;

segments.original: two or three lonely little freight piles scattered about the 'levee;' a pile of 'skids' on the slope of the stone-paved wharf, and the fragrant town drunkard asleep in the shadow of them;
segments.es: dos o tres montoncitos solitarios de carga esparcidos por el «dique»; una pila de «rampas» en la pendiente del muelle empedrado, y el fragante borracho del pueblo dormido a su sombra;
segments.en: two or three lonely little freight piles scattered about the 'levee;' a pile of 'skids' on the slope of the stone-paved wharf, and the fragrant town drunkard asleep in the shadow of them;

segments.original: two or three wood flats at the head of the wharf, but nobody to listen to the peaceful lapping of the wavelets against them;
segments.es: dos o tres barcazas de leña a la cabeza del muelle, pero nadie que escuchara el apacible chapoteo de las olitas contra ellas;
segments.en: two or three wood flats at the head of the wharf, but nobody to listen to the peaceful lapping of the wavelets against them;

segments.original: the great Mississippi, the majestic, the magnificent Mississippi, rolling its mile-wide tide along, shining in the sun;
segments.es: el gran Misisipi, el majestuoso, el magnífico Misisipi, arrastrando su corriente de una milla de ancho, brillando al sol;
segments.en: the great Mississippi, the majestic, the magnificent Mississippi, rolling its mile-wide tide along, shining in the sun;

segments.original: the dense forest away on the other side; the 'point' above the town, and the 'point' below, bounding the river-glimpse and turning it into a sort of sea, and withal a very still and brilliant and lonely one.
segments.es: el denso bosque allá en la otra orilla; la «punta» río arriba del pueblo y la «punta» río abajo, que cerraban la vista del río y la convertían en una especie de mar, y además muy quieto, brillante y solitario.
segments.en: the dense forest away on the other side; the 'point' above the town, and the 'point' below, bounding the river-glimpse and turning it into a sort of sea, and withal a very still and brilliant and lonely one.

segments.original: Presently a film of dark smoke appears above one of those remote 'points;' instantly a negro drayman, famous for his quick eye and prodigious voice, lifts up the cry, 'S-t-e-a-m-boat a-comin'!' and the scene changes!
segments.es: De pronto aparece un velo de humo oscuro sobre una de esas «puntas» lejanas; al instante un carretero negro, famoso por su vista rápida y su voz prodigiosa, lanza el grito: «¡Va-a-apor a la vista!», ¡y la escena cambia!
segments.en: Presently a film of dark smoke appears above one of those remote 'points;' instantly a negro drayman, famous for his quick eye and prodigious voice, lifts up the cry, 'S-t-e-a-m-boat a-comin'!' and the scene changes!

segments.original: The town drunkard stirs, the clerks wake up, a furious clatter of drays follows, every house and store pours out a human contribution, and all in a twinkling the dead town is alive and moving.
segments.es: El borracho del pueblo se mueve, los dependientes despiertan, sigue un furioso estrépito de carretas, cada casa y cada tienda vierte su contribución humana, y en un abrir y cerrar de ojos el pueblo muerto está vivo y en movimiento.
segments.en: The town drunkard stirs, the clerks wake up, a furious clatter of drays follows, every house and store pours out a human contribution, and all in a twinkling the dead town is alive and moving.

segments.original: Drays, carts, men, boys, all go hurrying from many quarters to a common center, the wharf.
segments.es: Carretas, carros, hombres, muchachos, todos corren desde muchos rincones hacia un centro común: el muelle.
segments.en: Drays, carts, men, boys, all go hurrying from many quarters to a common center, the wharf.

segments.original: Assembled there, the people fasten their eyes upon the coming boat as upon a wonder they are seeing for the first time. And the boat is rather a handsome sight, too.
segments.es: Reunida allí, la gente clava los ojos en el barco que llega como en una maravilla que viera por primera vez. Y el barco, a decir verdad, es bastante hermoso de ver.
segments.en: Assembled there, the people fasten their eyes upon the coming boat as upon a wonder they are seeing for the first time. And the boat is rather a handsome sight, too.

segments.original: She is long and sharp and trim and pretty; she has two tall, fancy-topped chimneys, with a gilded device of some kind swung between them;
segments.es: Es largo, afilado, esbelto y bonito; tiene dos chimeneas altas de remates vistosos, con algún emblema dorado colgado entre ellas;
segments.en: She is long and sharp and trim and pretty; she has two tall, fancy-topped chimneys, with a gilded device of some kind swung between them;

segments.original: a fanciful pilot-house, a glass and 'gingerbread', perched on top of the 'texas' deck behind them;
segments.es: una caprichosa cabina de pilotaje, toda cristal y «encaje de madera», encaramada sobre la cubierta «texas» detrás de ellas;
segments.en: a fanciful pilot-house, a glass and 'gingerbread', perched on top of the 'texas' deck behind them;

segments.original: the paddle-boxes are gorgeous with a picture or with gilded rays above the boat's name;
segments.es: las cajas de las ruedas lucen espléndidas con una pintura o con rayos dorados sobre el nombre del barco;
segments.en: the paddle-boxes are gorgeous with a picture or with gilded rays above the boat's name;

segments.original: the boiler deck, the hurricane deck, and the texas deck are fenced and ornamented with clean white railings;
segments.es: la cubierta de calderas, la cubierta superior y la cubierta texas están cercadas y adornadas con limpias barandillas blancas;
segments.en: the boiler deck, the hurricane deck, and the texas deck are fenced and ornamented with clean white railings;

segments.original: there is a flag gallantly flying from the jack-staff; the furnace doors are open and the fires glaring bravely; the upper decks are black with passengers;
segments.es: una bandera ondea gallarda en el asta de proa; las puertas de los hornos están abiertas y los fuegos arden con bravura; las cubiertas superiores están negras de pasajeros;
segments.en: there is a flag gallantly flying from the jack-staff; the furnace doors are open and the fires glaring bravely; the upper decks are black with passengers;

segments.original: the captain stands by the big bell, calm, imposing, the envy of all;
segments.es: el capitán está junto a la gran campana, sereno, imponente, envidia de todos;
segments.en: the captain stands by the big bell, calm, imposing, the envy of all;

segments.original: great volumes of the blackest smoke are rolling and tumbling out of the chimneys—a husbanded grandeur created with a bit of pitch pine just before arriving at a town;
segments.es: grandes masas del humo más negro salen rodando y revolviéndose de las chimeneas, una grandeza bien administrada, creada con un poco de pino resinoso justo antes de llegar a un pueblo;
segments.en: great volumes of the blackest smoke are rolling and tumbling out of the chimneys—a husbanded grandeur created with a bit of pitch pine just before arriving at a town;

segments.original: the crew are grouped on the forecastle; the broad stage is run far out over the port bow, and an envied deckhand stands picturesquely on the end of it with a coil of rope in his hand;
segments.es: la tripulación se agrupa en el castillo de proa; la ancha pasarela se tiende muy afuera sobre la amura de babor, y un envidiado marinero se yergue pintoresco en su extremo con un rollo de cuerda en la mano;
segments.en: the crew are grouped on the forecastle; the broad stage is run far out over the port bow, and an envied deckhand stands picturesquely on the end of it with a coil of rope in his hand;

segments.original: the pent steam is screaming through the gauge-cocks, the captain lifts his hand, a bell rings, the wheels stop; then they turn back, churning the water to foam, and the steamer is at rest.
segments.es: el vapor contenido chilla por las llaves de nivel, el capitán levanta la mano, suena una campana, las ruedas se detienen; luego giran hacia atrás, batiendo el agua hasta volverla espuma, y el vapor queda en reposo.
segments.en: the pent steam is screaming through the gauge-cocks, the captain lifts his hand, a bell rings, the wheels stop; then they turn back, churning the water to foam, and the steamer is at rest.

segments.original: Then such a scramble as there is to get aboard, and to get ashore, and to take in freight and to discharge freight, all at one and the same time; and such a yelling and cursing as the mates facilitate it all with!
segments.es: ¡Y entonces qué barullo para subir a bordo y bajar a tierra, para cargar y descargar mercancía, todo a la vez; y qué gritos y maldiciones con que los oficiales lo agilizan todo!
segments.en: Then such a scramble as there is to get aboard, and to get ashore, and to take in freight and to discharge freight, all at one and the same time; and such a yelling and cursing as the mates facilitate it all with!

segments.original: Ten minutes later the steamer is under way again, with no flag on the jack-staff and no black smoke issuing from the chimneys.
segments.es: Diez minutos después el vapor está otra vez en marcha, sin bandera en el asta de proa y sin humo negro saliendo de las chimeneas.
segments.en: Ten minutes later the steamer is under way again, with no flag on the jack-staff and no black smoke issuing from the chimneys.

segments.original: After ten more minutes the town is dead again, and the town drunkard asleep by the skids once more.
segments.es: Diez minutos más, y el pueblo está muerto otra vez, y el borracho del pueblo dormido junto a las rampas una vez más.
segments.en: After ten more minutes the town is dead again, and the town drunkard asleep by the skids once more.

works.author: Emma Lazarus
works.title: The New Colossus
works.scope: Complete sonnet · 14 lines
works.scope_es: Soneto completo · 14 versos
works.source_edition: English Wikisource, transcription of Lazarus’s 1883 manuscript, headed “Written in aid of Bartholdi Pedestal Fund”.
works.source_edition_es: Wikisource en inglés, transcripción del manuscrito de Lazarus de 1883, encabezado «Escrito en ayuda del fondo para el pedestal de Bartholdi».
works.note: Lazarus wrote the sonnet for an 1883 auction raising money for the statue’s pedestal. The “brazen giant” is the Colossus of Rhodes; the twin cities are New York and Brooklyn, still separate in 1883. In 1903 the poem was set on a bronze plaque inside the pedestal.
works.note_es: Lazarus escribió el soneto para una subasta de 1883 que recaudaba dinero para el pedestal de la estatua. El «gigante de bronce» es el Coloso de Rodas; las ciudades gemelas son Nueva York y Brooklyn, todavía separadas en 1883. En 1903 el poema se colocó en una placa de bronce dentro del pedestal.

segments.original: Not like the brazen giant of Greek fame,
segments.es: No como el gigante de bronce de fama griega,
segments.en: Not like the brazen giant of Greek fame,

segments.original: With conquering limbs astride from land to land;
segments.es: con miembros de conquistador a horcajadas de tierra en tierra;
segments.en: With conquering limbs astride from land to land;

segments.original: Here at our sea-washed, sunset gates shall stand
segments.es: aquí, en nuestras puertas del ocaso bañadas por el mar, se alzará
segments.en: Here at our sea-washed, sunset gates shall stand

segments.original: A mighty woman with a torch, whose flame
segments.es: una mujer poderosa con una antorcha, cuya llama
segments.en: A mighty woman with a torch, whose flame

segments.original: Is the imprisoned lightning, and her name
segments.es: es el relámpago aprisionado, y su nombre,
segments.en: Is the imprisoned lightning, and her name

segments.original: Mother of Exiles. From her beacon-hand
segments.es: Madre de los Desterrados. De su mano de faro
segments.en: Mother of Exiles. From her beacon-hand

segments.original: Glows world-wide welcome; her mild eyes command
segments.es: brilla una bienvenida para todo el mundo; sus ojos apacibles dominan
segments.en: Glows world-wide welcome; her mild eyes command

segments.original: The air-bridged harbor that twin cities frame.
segments.es: el puerto de puentes aéreos que enmarcan dos ciudades gemelas.
segments.en: The air-bridged harbor that twin cities frame.

segments.original: "Keep, ancient lands, your storied pomp!" cries she
segments.es: «¡Guardad, tierras antiguas, vuestra pompa legendaria!», clama ella
segments.en: "Keep, ancient lands, your storied pomp!" cries she

segments.original: With silent lips. "Give me your tired, your poor,
segments.es: con labios silenciosos. «Dadme a vuestros cansados, a vuestros pobres,
segments.en: With silent lips. "Give me your tired, your poor,

segments.original: Your huddled masses yearning to breathe free,
segments.es: a vuestras masas apiñadas que anhelan respirar libres,
segments.en: Your huddled masses yearning to breathe free,

segments.original: The wretched refuse of your teeming shore.
segments.es: el desecho miserable de vuestras costas rebosantes.
segments.en: The wretched refuse of your teeming shore.

segments.original: Send these, the homeless, tempest-tost to me,
segments.es: Enviadme a estos, los sin hogar, zarandeados por la tempestad:
segments.en: Send these, the homeless, tempest-tost to me,

segments.original: I lift my lamp beside the golden door!"
segments.es: ¡alzo mi lámpara junto a la puerta dorada!»
segments.en: I lift my lamp beside the golden door!"

works.author: Paul Laurence Dunbar
works.title: We Wear the Mask
works.scope: Complete poem · 15 lines
works.scope_es: Poema completo · 15 versos
works.source_edition: The Complete Poems of Paul Laurence Dunbar (1913), Project Gutenberg 18338; first published in Majors and Minors (1895). Double hyphen set as a dash.
works.source_edition_es: The Complete Poems of Paul Laurence Dunbar (1913), Project Gutenberg 18338; publicado por primera vez en Majors and Minors (1895). El guion doble se compone como raya.
works.note: Dunbar, the son of parents who had been enslaved in Kentucky, published the poem in his second book, printed at his own expense in Toledo, Ohio. It speaks for a “we” it never names; the last stanza turns to Christ.
works.note_es: Dunbar, hijo de padres que habían sido esclavizados en Kentucky, publicó el poema en su segundo libro, impreso a su costa en Toledo, Ohio. Habla por un «nosotros» que nunca nombra; la última estrofa se vuelve hacia Cristo.

segments.original: We wear the mask that grins and lies,
segments.es: Llevamos la máscara que sonríe y miente,
segments.en: We wear the mask that grins and lies,

segments.original: It hides our cheeks and shades our eyes,—
segments.es: que nos oculta las mejillas y nos vela los ojos:
segments.en: It hides our cheeks and shades our eyes,—

segments.original: This debt we pay to human guile;
segments.es: esta deuda pagamos a la astucia humana;
segments.en: This debt we pay to human guile;

segments.original: With torn and bleeding hearts we smile,
segments.es: con el corazón roto y sangrando sonreímos,
segments.en: With torn and bleeding hearts we smile,

segments.original: And mouth with myriad subtleties.
segments.es: y hablamos con mil sutilezas.
segments.en: And mouth with myriad subtleties.

segments.original: Why should the world be over-wise,
segments.es: ¿Por qué ha de ser el mundo tan sabio
segments.en: Why should the world be over-wise,

segments.original: In counting all our tears and sighs?
segments.es: que cuente todas nuestras lágrimas y suspiros?
segments.en: In counting all our tears and sighs?

segments.original: Nay, let them only see us, while
segments.es: No, que solo nos vean mientras
segments.en: Nay, let them only see us, while

segments.original: We wear the mask.
segments.es: llevamos la máscara.
segments.en: We wear the mask.

segments.original: We smile, but, O great Christ, our cries
segments.es: Sonreímos, pero, oh gran Cristo, nuestros gritos
segments.en: We smile, but, O great Christ, our cries

segments.original: To thee from tortured souls arise.
segments.es: suben hacia ti desde almas torturadas.
segments.en: To thee from tortured souls arise.

segments.original: We sing, but oh the clay is vile
segments.es: Cantamos, pero ay, el barro es vil
segments.en: We sing, but oh the clay is vile

segments.original: Beneath our feet, and long the mile;
segments.es: bajo nuestros pies, y larga la milla;
segments.en: Beneath our feet, and long the mile;

segments.original: But let the world dream otherwise,
segments.es: pero que el mundo sueñe otra cosa:
segments.en: But let the world dream otherwise,

segments.original: We wear the mask!
segments.es: ¡llevamos la máscara!
segments.en: We wear the mask!

works.author: Stephen Crane
works.title: A man said to the universe
works.title_es: Un hombre le dijo al universo
works.scope: War Is Kind · complete poem, 5 lines
works.scope_es: War Is Kind · poema completo, 5 versos
works.source_edition: Stephen Crane, War Is Kind (1899), Project Gutenberg 9870. The opening quotation mark of the last line is the book’s, marking the reply continued.
works.source_edition_es: Stephen Crane, War Is Kind (1899), Project Gutenberg 9870. La comilla con que empieza el último verso es del libro y marca que la respuesta continúa.
works.note: Crane, the son of a Methodist minister, published this poem in War Is Kind, a year before he died of tuberculosis at twenty-eight. The man’s claim and the universe’s answer are the whole poem.
works.note_es: Crane, hijo de un pastor metodista, publicó este poema en War Is Kind, un año antes de morir de tuberculosis a los veintiocho. La afirmación del hombre y la respuesta del universo son todo el poema.

segments.original: A man said to the universe:
segments.es: Un hombre le dijo al universo:
segments.en: A man said to the universe:

segments.original: "Sir, I exist!"
segments.es: «¡Señor, yo existo!»
segments.en: "Sir, I exist!"

segments.original: "However," replied the universe,
segments.es: «Sin embargo», respondió el universo,
segments.en: "However," replied the universe,

segments.original: "The fact has not created in me
segments.es: «ese hecho no ha creado en mí
segments.en: "The fact has not created in me

segments.original: "A sense of obligation."
segments.es: ningún sentido de obligación.»
segments.en: "A sense of obligation."

works.author: Edwin Markham
works.title: The Man with the Hoe
works.scope: Complete poem with its epigraph · 49 lines
works.scope_es: Poema completo con su epígrafe · 49 versos
works.source_edition: Edwin Markham, The Man with the Hoe, and Other Poems (1899), English Wikisource. The subtitle, “Written after seeing Millet’s World-Famous Painting”, is not set as a reading row.
works.source_edition_es: Edwin Markham, The Man with the Hoe, and Other Poems (1899), Wikisource en inglés. El subtítulo, «Escrito después de ver el famosísimo cuadro de Millet», no se compone como fila de lectura.
works.note: Markham, a school principal in Oakland, wrote the poem after seeing Millet’s painting in San Francisco. When the San Francisco Examiner printed it in January 1899, it was reprinted across the country within weeks.
works.note_es: Markham, director de una escuela en Oakland, escribió el poema después de ver el cuadro de Millet en San Francisco. Cuando el San Francisco Examiner lo publicó en enero de 1899, se reimprimió por todo el país en pocas semanas.

segments.original: God made man in His own image,
segments.es: Dios hizo al hombre a su imagen,
segments.en: God made man in His own image,

segments.original: in the image of God made He him.—Genesis.
segments.es: a imagen de Dios lo hizo. —Génesis.
segments.en: in the image of God made He him.—Genesis.

segments.original: Bowed by the weight of centuries he leans
segments.es: Encorvado por el peso de los siglos se apoya
segments.en: Bowed by the weight of centuries he leans

segments.original: Upon his hoe and gazes on the ground,
segments.es: en su azada y mira el suelo,
segments.en: Upon his hoe and gazes on the ground,

segments.original: The emptiness of ages in his face,
segments.es: el vacío de las eras en el rostro,
segments.en: The emptiness of ages in his face,

segments.original: And on his back the burden of the world.
segments.es: y sobre la espalda la carga del mundo.
segments.en: And on his back the burden of the world.

segments.original: Who made him dead to rapture and despair,
segments.es: ¿Quién lo hizo muerto al éxtasis y a la desesperación,
segments.en: Who made him dead to rapture and despair,

segments.original: A thing that grieves not and that never hopes,
segments.es: una cosa que no se aflige y que nunca espera,
segments.en: A thing that grieves not and that never hopes,

segments.original: Stolid and stunned, a brother to the ox?
segments.es: impasible y aturdido, hermano del buey?
segments.en: Stolid and stunned, a brother to the ox?

segments.original: Who loosened and let down this brutal jaw?
segments.es: ¿Quién aflojó y dejó caer esta mandíbula brutal?
segments.en: Who loosened and let down this brutal jaw?

segments.original: Whose was the hand that slanted back this brow?
segments.es: ¿De quién fue la mano que echó hacia atrás esta frente?
segments.en: Whose was the hand that slanted back this brow?

segments.original: Whose breath blew out the light within this brain?
segments.es: ¿De quién el aliento que apagó la luz dentro de este cerebro?
segments.en: Whose breath blew out the light within this brain?

segments.original: Is this the Thing the Lord God made and gave
segments.es: ¿Es esta la Cosa que el Señor Dios hizo y a la que dio
segments.en: Is this the Thing the Lord God made and gave

segments.original: To have dominion over sea and land;
segments.es: dominio sobre el mar y la tierra;
segments.en: To have dominion over sea and land;

segments.original: To trace the stars and search the heavens for power;
segments.es: para seguir las estrellas y buscar en los cielos el poder;
segments.en: To trace the stars and search the heavens for power;

segments.original: To feel the passion of Eternity?
segments.es: para sentir la pasión de la Eternidad?
segments.en: To feel the passion of Eternity?

segments.original: Is this the Dream He dreamed who shaped the suns
segments.es: ¿Es este el Sueño que soñó Aquel que dio forma a los soles
segments.en: Is this the Dream He dreamed who shaped the suns

segments.original: And pillared the blue firmament with light?
segments.es: y sostuvo con columnas de luz el firmamento azul?
segments.en: And pillared the blue firmament with light?

segments.original: Down all the stretch of Hell to its last gulf
segments.es: En toda la extensión del Infierno, hasta su último abismo,
segments.en: Down all the stretch of Hell to its last gulf

segments.original: There is no shape more terrible than this—
segments.es: no hay figura más terrible que esta,
segments.en: There is no shape more terrible than this—

segments.original: More tongued with censure of the world's blind greed—
segments.es: que hable más alto contra la ciega codicia del mundo,
segments.en: More tongued with censure of the world's blind greed—

segments.original: More filled with signs and portents for the soul—
segments.es: más llena de señales y presagios para el alma,
segments.en: More filled with signs and portents for the soul—

segments.original: More fraught with menace to the universe.
segments.es: más cargada de amenaza para el universo.
segments.en: More fraught with menace to the universe.

segments.original: What gulfs between him and the seraphim!
segments.es: ¡Qué abismos entre él y los serafines!
segments.en: What gulfs between him and the seraphim!

segments.original: Slave of the wheel of labor, what to him
segments.es: Esclavo de la rueda del trabajo, ¿qué son para él
segments.en: Slave of the wheel of labor, what to him

segments.original: Are Plato and the swing of Pleiades?
segments.es: Platón y el giro de las Pléyades?
segments.en: Are Plato and the swing of Pleiades?

segments.original: What the long reaches of the peaks of song,
segments.es: ¿Qué, las largas extensiones de las cumbres del canto,
segments.en: What the long reaches of the peaks of song,

segments.original: The rift of dawn, the reddening of the rose?
segments.es: la grieta del alba, el enrojecer de la rosa?
segments.en: The rift of dawn, the reddening of the rose?

segments.original: Through this dread shape the suffering ages look;
segments.es: A través de esta figura temible miran las edades dolientes;
segments.en: Through this dread shape the suffering ages look;

segments.original: Time's tragedy is in that aching stoop;
segments.es: la tragedia del Tiempo está en esa espalda doliente y encorvada;
segments.en: Time's tragedy is in that aching stoop;

segments.original: Through this dread shape humanity betrayed,
segments.es: a través de esta figura temible la humanidad traicionada,
segments.en: Through this dread shape humanity betrayed,

segments.original: Plundered, profaned and disinherited,
segments.es: saqueada, profanada y desheredada,
segments.en: Plundered, profaned and disinherited,

segments.original: Cries protest to the Judges of the World,
segments.es: clama su protesta ante los Jueces del Mundo,
segments.en: Cries protest to the Judges of the World,

segments.original: A protest that is also prophecy.
segments.es: una protesta que es también profecía.
segments.en: A protest that is also prophecy.

segments.original: O masters, lords, and rulers in all lands,
segments.es: Oh amos, señores y gobernantes de todas las tierras,
segments.en: O masters, lords, and rulers in all lands,

segments.original: Is this the handiwork you give to God,
segments.es: ¿es esta la obra de vuestras manos que entregáis a Dios,
segments.en: Is this the handiwork you give to God,

segments.original: This monstrous thing distorted and soul-quenched?
segments.es: esta cosa monstruosa, deformada y con el alma apagada?
segments.en: This monstrous thing distorted and soul-quenched?

segments.original: How will you ever straighten up this shape;
segments.es: ¿Cómo enderezaréis alguna vez esta figura,
segments.en: How will you ever straighten up this shape;

segments.original: Touch it again with immortality;
segments.es: la tocaréis otra vez con la inmortalidad,
segments.en: Touch it again with immortality;

segments.original: Give back the upward looking and the light;
segments.es: le devolveréis la mirada hacia lo alto y la luz,
segments.en: Give back the upward looking and the light;

segments.original: Rebuild in it the music and the dream;
segments.es: reconstruiréis en ella la música y el sueño,
segments.en: Rebuild in it the music and the dream;

segments.original: Make right the immemorial infamies,
segments.es: repararéis las infamias inmemoriales,
segments.en: Make right the immemorial infamies,

segments.original: Perfidious wrongs, immedicable woes?
segments.es: los agravios pérfidos, los males sin remedio?
segments.en: Perfidious wrongs, immedicable woes?

segments.original: O masters, lords, and rulers in all lands,
segments.es: Oh amos, señores y gobernantes de todas las tierras,
segments.en: O masters, lords, and rulers in all lands,

segments.original: How will the Future reckon with this Man?
segments.es: ¿cómo ajustará cuentas el Futuro con este Hombre?
segments.en: How will the Future reckon with this Man?

segments.original: How answer his brute question in that hour
segments.es: ¿Cómo responder a su pregunta bruta en aquella hora
segments.en: How answer his brute question in that hour

segments.original: When whirlwinds of rebellion shake the world?
segments.es: en que torbellinos de rebelión sacudan el mundo?
segments.en: When whirlwinds of rebellion shake the world?

segments.original: How will it be with kingdoms and with kings—
segments.es: ¿Qué será de los reinos y de los reyes,
segments.en: How will it be with kingdoms and with kings—

segments.original: With those who shaped him to the thing he is—
segments.es: de quienes lo moldearon hasta hacerlo lo que es,
segments.en: With those who shaped him to the thing he is—

segments.original: When this dumb Terror shall reply to God,
segments.es: cuando este Terror mudo responda a Dios
segments.en: When this dumb Terror shall reply to God,

segments.original: After the silence of the centuries?
segments.es: después del silencio de los siglos?
segments.en: After the silence of the centuries?

works.author: Aeschylus
works.title: Learning through suffering
works.scope: Agamemnon, 160–183 · the Hymn to Zeus, complete
works.scope_es: Agamenón, 160-183 · el himno a Zeus, completo
works.source_edition: Aeschylus, Agamemnon, ed. Herbert Weir Smyth (Loeb, 1926), Perseus Digital Library TEI text. Line numbers as in the edition, which prints no lines 169 and 174; the words divided across verse ends are kept divided.
works.source_edition_es: Esquilo, Agamenón, ed. de Herbert Weir Smyth (Loeb, 1926), texto TEI de la Perseus Digital Library. Numeración de la edición, que no imprime los versos 169 y 174; las palabras partidas entre dos versos se conservan partidas.
works.note: Agamemnon opened the Oresteia at the Dionysia of 458 BC. The old men of Argos, waiting for the king’s return from Troy, turn to Zeus: he has made it law that mortals learn through suffering, and that wisdom comes even to the unwilling.
works.note_es: Agamenón abrió la Orestíada en las Dionisias del 458 a. C. Los ancianos de Argos, que esperan el regreso del rey desde Troya, se vuelven hacia Zeus: él ha hecho ley que los mortales aprendan sufriendo, y que la cordura llegue aun a quien no la quiere.

segments.original: Ζεύς, ὅστις ποτʼ ἐστίν, εἰ τόδʼ αὐ-
segments.es: Zeus, quienquiera que sea, si con este
segments.en: Zeus, whoever he may be, if by this

segments.original: τῷ φίλον κεκλημένῳ,
segments.es: nombre le agrada ser llamado,
segments.en: name it pleases him to be called,

segments.original: τοῦτό νιν προσεννέπω.
segments.es: con este lo invoco.
segments.en: by this name I call on him.

segments.original: οὐκ ἔχω προσεικάσαι
segments.es: No tengo con qué compararlo,
segments.en: I have nothing to liken him to,

segments.original: πάντʼ ἐπισταθμώμενος
segments.es: aunque lo sopese todo,
segments.en: though I weigh all things,

segments.original: πλὴν Διός, εἰ τὸ μάταν ἀπὸ φροντίδος ἄχθος
segments.es: salvo a Zeus, si la vana carga de la inquietud
segments.en: except Zeus, if the vain burden of my anxious mind

segments.original: χρὴ βαλεῖν ἐτητύμως.
segments.es: he de arrojar de veras.
segments.en: is truly to be cast away.

segments.original: οὐδʼ ὅστις πάροιθεν ἦν μέγας,
segments.es: Ni aquel que antes fue grande,
segments.en: Not even he who once was great,

segments.original: παμμάχῳ θράσει βρύων,
segments.es: rebosante de audacia para toda lucha,
segments.en: bursting with boldness for every fight,

segments.original: οὐδὲ λέξεται πρὶν ὤν·
segments.es: será nombrado siquiera, pues ya pasó;
segments.en: will be so much as named, for he is past;

segments.original: ὃς δʼ ἔπειτʼ ἔφυ, τρια-
segments.es: y el que vino después encontró
segments.en: and he who came after met

segments.original: κτῆρος οἴχεται τυχών.
segments.es: a su vencedor y se fue.
segments.en: his conqueror and is gone.

segments.original: Ζῆνα δέ τις προφρόνως ἐπινίκια κλάζων
segments.es: Pero quien de buen grado cante a Zeus el canto de victoria
segments.en: But whoever gladly sings the victory song to Zeus

segments.original: τεύξεται φρενῶν τὸ πᾶν·
segments.es: alcanzará la sabiduría entera:
segments.en: will win wisdom entire:

segments.original: τὸν φρονεῖν βροτοὺς ὁδώ-
segments.es: a él, que puso a los mortales en el camino
segments.en: Zeus, who set mortals on the road

segments.original: σαντα, τὸν πάθει μάθος
segments.es: del saber, que estableció que aprender sufriendo
segments.en: to understanding, who laid down that learning through suffering

segments.original: θέντα κυρίως ἔχειν.
segments.es: tuviera plena autoridad.
segments.en: should hold with full authority.

segments.original: στάζει δʼ ἔν θʼ ὕπνῳ πρὸ καρδίας
segments.es: Gotea en el sueño, ante el corazón,
segments.en: In sleep there drips before the heart

segments.original: μνησιπήμων πόνος· καὶ παρʼ ἄ-
segments.es: la pena que recuerda el daño; y aun a los que
segments.en: the pain that remembers harm; and even to the

segments.original: κοντας ἦλθε σωφρονεῖν.
segments.es: no lo quieren les llega la cordura.
segments.en: unwilling wisdom comes.

segments.original: δαιμόνων δέ που χάρις βίαιος
segments.es: Violenta es, sin duda, la gracia de los dioses
segments.en: Violent, surely, is the grace of the gods

segments.original: σέλμα σεμνὸν ἡμένων.
segments.es: sentados en su sagrado banco de timón.
segments.en: who sit at the holy helm.

works.author: Sophocles
works.title: Call no one happy
works.scope: Oedipus the King, 1524–1530 · the closing lines, complete
works.scope_es: Edipo rey, 1524-1530 · los versos finales, completos
works.source_edition: Sophocles, Oedipus Tyrannus, ed. Francis Storr (Loeb, 1912), Perseus Digital Library TEI text, which gives the lines to the Chorus.
works.source_edition_es: Sófocles, Edipo rey, ed. de Francis Storr (Loeb, 1912), texto TEI de la Perseus Digital Library, que atribuye los versos al coro.
works.note: The last words of the play, after Oedipus has blinded himself and asked to be sent from Thebes. The man who solved the Sphinx’s riddle becomes the example of the old Greek saying: count no one happy until the end.
works.note_es: Las últimas palabras de la obra, después de que Edipo se ha cegado y ha pedido que lo expulsen de Tebas. El hombre que resolvió el enigma de la Esfinge se vuelve el ejemplo del viejo dicho griego: no llames feliz a nadie antes del final.

segments.original: ὦ πάτρας Θήβης ἔνοικοι, λεύσσετʼ, Οἰδίπους ὅδε,
segments.es: Habitantes de Tebas, mi patria, mirad: este es Edipo,
segments.en: Dwellers in our native Thebes, behold: this is Oedipus,

segments.original: ὃς τὰ κλείνʼ αἰνίγματʼ ᾔδει καὶ κράτιστος ἦν ἀνήρ,
segments.es: que conocía el famoso enigma y fue el más poderoso de los hombres,
segments.en: who knew the famous riddle and was a man most mighty,

segments.original: οὗ τίς οὐ ζήλῳ πολιτῶν ἦν τύχαις ἐπιβλέπων,
segments.es: cuya fortuna ¿qué ciudadano no miraba con envidia?,
segments.en: on whose fortunes what citizen did not look with envy?

segments.original: εἰς ὅσον κλύδωνα δεινῆς συμφορᾶς ἐλήλυθεν.
segments.es: ¡a qué oleaje de terrible desgracia ha llegado!
segments.en: Into what a sea of dire misfortune he has come!

segments.original: ὥστε θνητὸν ὄντα κείνην τὴν τελευταίαν ἰδεῖν
segments.es: Así pues, siendo mortal, con la mirada puesta en aquel último
segments.en: So, being mortal, keep your eyes on that last

segments.original: ἡμέραν ἐπισκοποῦντα μηδένʼ ὀλβίζειν, πρὶν ἂν
segments.es: día, no llames feliz a nadie antes de que
segments.en: day, and call no one happy until

segments.original: τέρμα τοῦ βίου περάσῃ μηδὲν ἀλγεινὸν παθών.
segments.es: haya cruzado el término de la vida sin sufrir dolor.
segments.en: he has crossed the bound of life without suffering pain.

works.author: Euripides
works.title: Medea before her children
works.scope: Medea, 1021–1080 · the monologue, complete
works.scope_es: Medea, 1021-1080 · el monólogo, completo
works.source_edition: Euripides, Medea, ed. Gilbert Murray (Oxford, 1902), Perseus Digital Library TEI text.
works.source_edition_es: Eurípides, Medea, ed. de Gilbert Murray (Oxford, 1902), texto TEI de la Perseus Digital Library.
works.note: Jason has left Medea to marry the king’s daughter, and Medea has sent the bride a poisoned robe and crown. Now, with her sons in front of her, she changes her mind and changes it back. The last three lines are among the most quoted in Greek tragedy: she knows what she is about to do, and passion is stronger.
works.note_es: Jasón ha dejado a Medea para casarse con la hija del rey, y Medea ha enviado a la novia un peplo y una corona envenenados. Ahora, con sus hijos delante, cambia de idea y vuelve a cambiarla. Los tres últimos versos están entre los más citados de la tragedia griega: sabe lo que va a hacer, y la pasión es más fuerte.

segments.original: ὦ τέκνα τέκνα, σφῷν μὲν ἔστι δὴ πόλις
segments.es: ¡Hijos, hijos!, vosotros tenéis una ciudad
segments.en: O children, children, you have a city

segments.original: καὶ δῶμ’, ἐν ᾧ, λιπόντες ἀθλίαν ἐμέ,
segments.es: y una casa donde, dejándome a mí, desdichada,
segments.en: and a home where, leaving me in my misery,

segments.original: οἰκήσετ’ αἰεὶ μητρὸς ἐστερημένοι·
segments.es: viviréis siempre privados de vuestra madre;
segments.en: you will live forever without your mother;

segments.original: ἐγὼ δ’ ἐς ἄλλην γαῖαν εἶμι δὴ φυγάς,
segments.es: y yo me voy desterrada a otra tierra
segments.en: and I go an exile to another land

segments.original: πρὶν σφῷν ὀνάσθαι κἀπιδεῖν εὐδαίμονας,
segments.es: antes de gozar de vosotros y veros felices,
segments.en: before I have had joy of you and seen you happy,

segments.original: πρὶν λέκτρα καὶ γυναῖκα καὶ γαμηλίους
segments.es: antes de adornar vuestros lechos, a la esposa y el tálamo
segments.en: before I have dressed your wedding beds, your brides and bridal

segments.original: εὐνὰς ἀγῆλαι λαμπάδας τ’ ἀνασχεθεῖν.
segments.es: nupcial, y de alzar las antorchas.
segments.en: chambers, and held the torches high.

segments.original: ὦ δυστάλαινα τῆς ἐμῆς αὐθαδίας.
segments.es: ¡Oh desdichada de mí por mi obstinación!
segments.en: O wretched me, for my own stubborn will!

segments.original: ἄλλως ἄρ’ ὑμᾶς, ὦ τέκν’, ἐξεθρεψάμην,
segments.es: En vano, hijos, os crié,
segments.en: In vain, then, children, did I raise you,

segments.original: ἄλλως δ’ ἐμόχθουν καὶ κατεξάνθην πόνοις,
segments.es: en vano me afané y me consumí en fatigas,
segments.en: in vain I toiled and was worn away with labour,

segments.original: στερρὰς ἐνεγκοῦσ’ ἐν τόκοις ἀλγηδόνας.
segments.es: tras sufrir en los partos duros dolores.
segments.en: bearing hard pangs in childbirth.

segments.original: ἦ μήν ποθ’ ἡ δύστηνος εἶχον ἐλπίδας
segments.es: Yo, desdichada, tenía de verdad muchas esperanzas
segments.en: Truly once I, poor wretch, had many hopes

segments.original: πολλὰς ἐν ὑμῖν, γηροβοσκήσειν τ’ ἐμὲ
segments.es: puestas en vosotros: que me cuidaríais en la vejez
segments.en: in you: that you would care for me in old age

segments.original: καὶ κατθανοῦσαν χερσὶν εὖ περιστελεῖν,
segments.es: y, al morir, me amortajaríais bien con vuestras manos,
segments.en: and, when I died, lay me out well with your own hands,

segments.original: ζηλωτὸν ἀνθρώποισι· νῦν δ’ ὄλωλε δὴ
segments.es: algo envidiable para los hombres; pero ahora ha muerto
segments.en: a thing all people envy; but now it has perished,

segments.original: γλυκεῖα φροντίς. σφῷν γὰρ ἐστερημένη
segments.es: ese dulce pensamiento. Pues privada de vosotros
segments.en: that sweet thought. For without you

segments.original: λυπρὸν διάξω βίοτον ἀλγεινόν τ’ ἐμοί.
segments.es: pasaré una vida triste y dolorosa.
segments.en: I shall live out a life of grief and pain.

segments.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ μητέρ’ οὐκέτ’ ὄμμασιν φίλοις
segments.es: Y vosotros ya no veréis a vuestra madre con ojos
segments.en: And you will no longer see your mother with loving

segments.original: ὄψεσθ’, ἐς ἄλλο σχῆμ’ ἀποστάντες βίου.
segments.es: queridos, idos a otra forma de vida.
segments.en: eyes, gone off into another shape of life.

segments.original: φεῦ φεῦ· τί προσδέρκεσθέ μ’ ὄμμασιν, τέκνα;
segments.es: ¡Ay, ay! ¿Por qué me miráis así, hijos?
segments.en: Alas, alas: why do you look at me so, children?

segments.original: τί προσγελᾶτε τὸν πανύστατον γέλων;
segments.es: ¿Por qué me sonreís con la última de las sonrisas?
segments.en: Why do you smile at me that last of all smiles?

segments.original: αἰαῖ· τί δράσω; καρδία γὰρ οἴχεται,
segments.es: ¡Ay! ¿Qué haré? Pues el corazón se me va,
segments.en: Ah, what shall I do? My heart fails me,

segments.original: γυναῖκες, ὄμμα φαιδρὸν ὡς εἶδον τέκνων.
segments.es: mujeres, al ver la mirada radiante de mis hijos.
segments.en: women, when I see the bright faces of my children.

segments.original: οὐκ ἂν δυναίμην· χαιρέτω βουλεύματα
segments.es: No podría. ¡Adiós a mis planes
segments.en: I could not do it. Farewell to my plans

segments.original: τὰ πρόσθεν· ἄξω παῖδας ἐκ γαίας ἐμούς.
segments.es: de antes! Me llevaré a mis hijos de esta tierra.
segments.en: of before: I will take my children out of this land.

segments.original: τί δεῖ με πατέρα τῶνδε τοῖς τούτων κακοῖς
segments.es: ¿Por qué he de causar dolor a su padre con los males de ellos
segments.en: Why should I, to hurt their father with their suffering,

segments.original: λυποῦσαν αὐτὴν δὶς τόσα κτᾶσθαι κακά;
segments.es: y ganarme yo misma el doble de males?
segments.en: win for myself twice as much suffering?

segments.original: οὐ δῆτ’ ἔγωγε. χαιρέτω βουλεύματα.
segments.es: No, yo no. ¡Adiós a mis planes!
segments.en: Not I, no. Farewell to my plans.

segments.original: καίτοι τί πάσχω; βούλομαι γέλωτ’ ὀφλεῖν
segments.es: Y sin embargo, ¿qué me pasa? ¿Quiero ser objeto de burla
segments.en: And yet what is happening to me? Do I want to be mocked,

segments.original: ἐχθροὺς μεθεῖσα τοὺς ἐμοὺς ἀζημίους;
segments.es: dejando sin castigo a mis enemigos?
segments.en: letting my enemies go unpunished?

segments.original: τολμητέον τάδ’. ἀλλὰ τῆς ἐμῆς κάκης,
segments.es: Hay que atreverse. ¡Qué cobardía la mía,
segments.en: I must dare it. What cowardice of mine,

segments.original: τὸ καὶ προσέσθαι μαλθακοὺς λόγους φρενί.
segments.es: dejar entrar siquiera en mi mente palabras blandas!
segments.en: even to let soft words into my mind!

segments.original: χωρεῖτε, παῖδες, ἐς δόμους. ὅτῳ δὲ μὴ
segments.es: Entrad en casa, hijos. Y a quien no
segments.en: Go into the house, children. And whoever

segments.original: θέμις παρεῖναι τοῖς ἐμοῖσι θύμασιν,
segments.es: le sea lícito asistir a mis sacrificios,
segments.en: may not rightly be present at my sacrifice,

segments.original: αὐτῷ μελήσει· χεῖρα δ’ οὐ διαφθερῶ.
segments.es: que se cuide él; mi mano no vacilará.
segments.en: let him see to it: my hand will not falter.

segments.original: ἆ ἆ.
segments.es: ¡Ah, ah!
segments.en: Ah, ah!

segments.original: μὴ δῆτα, θυμέ, μὴ σύ γ’ ἐργάσῃ τάδε·
segments.es: ¡No, corazón mío, no hagas tú esto!
segments.en: No, my heart, do not you do this!

segments.original: ἔασον αὐτούς, ὦ τάλαν, φεῖσαι τέκνων·
segments.es: Déjalos, desdichado, perdona a los hijos;
segments.en: Let them be, poor heart, spare the children;

segments.original: ἐκεῖ μεθ’ ἡμῶν ζῶντες εὐφρανοῦσί σε.
segments.es: allá, viviendo con nosotros, te alegrarán.
segments.en: living with us there, they will gladden you.

segments.original: μὰ τοὺς παρ’ Ἅιδῃ νερτέρους ἀλάστορας,
segments.es: ¡No, por los vengadores de abajo, junto a Hades!,
segments.en: No, by the avenging spirits below with Hades,

segments.original: οὔτοι ποτ’ ἔσται τοῦθ’ ὅπως ἐχθροῖς ἐγὼ
segments.es: jamás sucederá que yo
segments.en: it shall never be that I

segments.original: παῖδας παρήσω τοὺς ἐμοὺς καθυβρίσαι.
segments.es: deje a mis hijos al ultraje de mis enemigos.
segments.en: leave my children for my enemies to outrage.

segments.original: πάντως σφ’ ἀνάγκη κατθανεῖν· ἐπεὶ δὲ χρή,
segments.es: De todos modos tienen que morir; y puesto que es preciso,
segments.en: In any case they must die; and since they must,

segments.original: ἡμεῖς κτενοῦμεν οἵπερ ἐξεφύσαμεν.
segments.es: los mataré yo, que los di a luz.
segments.en: I who gave them birth will kill them.

segments.original: πάντως πέπρακται ταῦτα κοὐκ ἐκφεύξεται.
segments.es: Todo está hecho ya, y no hay escapatoria.
segments.en: It is all done, and there is no escape.

segments.original: καὶ δὴ ’πὶ κρατὶ στέφανος, ἐν πέπλοισι δὲ
segments.es: Ya tiene la corona en la cabeza, y en el peplo
segments.en: Already the crown is on her head, and in the robe

segments.original: νύμφη τύραννος ὄλλυται, σάφ’ οἶδ’ ἐγώ.
segments.es: la novia real se muere, bien lo sé.
segments.en: the royal bride is dying, I know it well.

segments.original: ἀλλ’, εἶμι γὰρ δὴ τλημονεστάτην ὁδόν,
segments.es: Pero, pues voy por el camino más cruel
segments.en: But since I go the cruellest road,

segments.original: καὶ τούσδε πέμψω τλημονεστέραν ἔτι,
segments.es: y a estos los enviaré por uno más cruel todavía,
segments.en: and will send these on one crueller still,

segments.original: παῖδας προσειπεῖν βούλομαι.—δότ’, ὦ τέκνα,
segments.es: quiero despedirme de mis hijos. Dadme, hijos,
segments.en: I want to say goodbye to my children. Give, children,

segments.original: δότ’ ἀσπάσασθαι μητρὶ δεξιὰν χέρα.
segments.es: dadle a vuestra madre la mano derecha para besarla.
segments.en: give your mother your right hand to kiss.

segments.original: ὦ φιλτάτη χείρ, φίλτατον δέ μοι στόμα
segments.es: ¡Oh mano queridísima, boca queridísima para mí,
segments.en: O dearest hand, and mouth most dear to me,

segments.original: καὶ σχῆμα καὶ πρόσωπον εὐγενὲς τέκνων,
segments.es: y figura y noble rostro de mis hijos,
segments.en: and form and noble face of my children,

segments.original: εὐδαιμονοῖτον, ἀλλ’ ἐκεῖ· τὰ δ’ ἐνθάδε
segments.es: sed felices, pero allá; lo de aquí
segments.en: be happy, but there: what was here

segments.original: πατὴρ ἀφείλετ’. ὦ γλυκεῖα προσβολή,
segments.es: os lo quitó vuestro padre. ¡Oh dulce abrazo,
segments.en: your father took away. O sweet embrace,

segments.original: ὦ μαλθακὸς χρὼς πνεῦμά θ’ ἥδιστον τέκνων.
segments.es: oh piel suave y dulcísimo aliento de mis hijos!
segments.en: O soft skin and sweetest breath of my children!

segments.original: χωρεῖτε χωρεῖτ’· οὐκέτ’ εἰμὶ προσβλέπειν
segments.es: ¡Id, id! Ya no soy capaz de miraros
segments.en: Go, go: I can no longer bear to look

segments.original: οἵα τε πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἀλλὰ νικῶμαι κακοῖς.
segments.es: a la cara, sino que me vencen los males.
segments.en: at you, but I am overcome by evils.

segments.original: καὶ μανθάνω μὲν οἷα δρᾶν μέλλω κακά,
segments.es: Y comprendo qué males voy a hacer,
segments.en: And I understand what evils I am about to do,

segments.original: θυμὸς δὲ κρείσσων τῶν ἐμῶν βουλευμάτων,
segments.es: pero mi furia es más fuerte que mis razones,
segments.en: but my passion is stronger than my reasoning,

segments.original: ὅσπερ μεγίστων αἴτιος κακῶν βροτοῖς.
segments.es: la furia, causa de los mayores males para los mortales.
segments.en: passion, which brings the greatest evils on mortals.

works.author: William Shakespeare
works.title: Speak of me as I am
works.title_es: Hablad de mí tal como soy

works.source_edition: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare, Project Gutenberg 100. This text reads “base Judean”, as the First Folio does; the 1622 Quarto has “base Indian”. The stage direction is set in brackets without italics.
works.source_edition_es: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare, Project Gutenberg 100. Este texto lee «base Judean», como el Primer Folio; el Cuarto de 1622 dice «base Indian». La acotación se compone entre corchetes, sin cursiva.
works.note: Othello has killed Desdemona, and has just learned that Iago deceived him. Before the Venetian envoys take him away he asks them to tell the story as it was, then uses on himself the words Venice used for its enemies.
works.note_es: Otelo ha matado a Desdémona y acaba de saber que Yago lo engañó. Antes de que los enviados de Venecia se lo lleven, les pide que cuenten la historia tal como fue, y luego usa contra sí mismo las palabras con que Venecia nombraba a sus enemigos.

segments.original: Soft you; a word or two before you go.
segments.es: Esperad; una palabra o dos antes de que os vayáis.
segments.en: Soft you; a word or two before you go.

segments.original: I have done the state some service, and they know’t.
segments.es: He prestado algún servicio al Estado, y ellos lo saben.
segments.en: I have done the state some service, and they know’t.

segments.original: No more of that. I pray you, in your letters,
segments.es: Pero basta de eso. Os ruego que en vuestras cartas,
segments.en: No more of that. I pray you, in your letters,

segments.original: When you shall these unlucky deeds relate,
segments.es: cuando relatéis estos hechos desdichados,
segments.en: When you shall these unlucky deeds relate,

segments.original: Speak of me as I am. Nothing extenuate,
segments.es: habléis de mí tal como soy. No atenuéis nada,
segments.en: Speak of me as I am. Nothing extenuate,

segments.original: Nor set down aught in malice. Then must you speak
segments.es: ni escribáis nada con malicia. Entonces habréis de hablar
segments.en: Nor set down aught in malice. Then must you speak

segments.original: Of one that loved not wisely, but too well;
segments.es: de uno que amó no con prudencia, sino demasiado;
segments.en: Of one that loved not wisely, but too well;

segments.original: Of one not easily jealous, but being wrought,
segments.es: de uno que no se ponía celoso fácilmente, pero que, una vez trabajado,
segments.en: Of one not easily jealous, but being wrought,

segments.original: Perplex’d in the extreme; of one whose hand,
segments.es: se perturbó hasta el extremo; de uno cuya mano,
segments.en: Perplex’d in the extreme; of one whose hand,

segments.original: Like the base Judean, threw a pearl away
segments.es: como el vil judío, arrojó una perla
segments.en: Like the base Judean, threw a pearl away

segments.original: Richer than all his tribe; of one whose subdu’d eyes,
segments.es: más valiosa que toda su tribu; de uno cuyos ojos vencidos,
segments.en: Richer than all his tribe; of one whose subdu’d eyes,

segments.original: Albeit unused to the melting mood,
segments.es: aunque no acostumbrados a enternecerse,
segments.en: Albeit unused to the melting mood,

segments.original: Drop tears as fast as the Arabian trees
segments.es: derraman lágrimas tan deprisa como los árboles de Arabia
segments.en: Drop tears as fast as the Arabian trees

segments.original: Their medicinal gum. Set you down this.
segments.es: su goma medicinal. Escribid esto.
segments.en: Their medicinal gum. Set you down this.

segments.original: And say besides, that in Aleppo once,
segments.es: Y decid además que una vez, en Alepo,
segments.en: And say besides, that in Aleppo once,

segments.original: Where a malignant and a turban’d Turk
segments.es: donde un turco maligno, con turbante,
segments.en: Where a malignant and a turban’d Turk

segments.original: Beat a Venetian and traduc’d the state,
segments.es: golpeó a un veneciano e injurió al Estado,
segments.en: Beat a Venetian and traduc’d the state,

segments.original: I took by the throat the circumcised dog,
segments.es: agarré por el cuello al perro circuncidado
segments.en: I took by the throat the circumcised dog,

segments.original: And smote him, thus.
segments.es: y lo herí, así.
segments.en: And smote him, thus.

segments.original: [Stabs himself.]
segments.es: [Se apuñala.]
segments.en: [Stabs himself.]
